f your lower belly is the one area that never seems to tighten up, it may not just be about doing more crunches. For many women, that lower belly area is affected by more than just ab training. Pelvic floor function, deep core activation, breathing mechanics, hormones, and overall nutrition all play a role. If those foundations are off, piling on more ab work often will not give you the result you want. What actually matters: ✨ Healing and strengthening the pelvic floor ✨ Building deep core control before advanced ab work ✨ Supporting your body with consistent nutrition ✨ Understanding that female physiology matters And remember: if your goal is fat loss, that comes from a calorie deficit. You cannot spot reduce lower belly fat with ab exercises alone. Core work helps strengthen the muscles underneath, but lasting change comes from working with your body, not against it. O segredo de BÍCEPS GIGANTES 👀Leia👇 👉Se o seu braço parece “fino” na vista lateral… talvez o problema não seja o bíceps 👀 O músculo braquial fica literalmente “embaixo” do bíceps braquial e, quando bem desenvolvido, ajuda a empurrar o bíceps pra cima, aumentando a sensação de espessura do braço, principalmente de lado. E é aí que entram exercícios como: • Rosca martelo • Rosca com pegada invertida • Rosca martelo cruzando no ombro oposto Cada um deles muda a posição da mão e do antebraço, alterando a participação dos flexores do cotovelo e aumentando o recrutamento de músculos como braquial e braquiorradial. Mas lembre: não existe exercício mágico e nem execução perfeita. O que gera hipertrofia continua sendo consistência, progressão de carga, volume bem ajustado e individualização. Variar pegadas e estímulos pode ser uma ótima estratégia pra desenvolvimento completo do braço 💪 Referências bibliográficas: • Coratella G. et al. “Biceps Brachii and Brachioradialis Excitation in Biceps Curl Exercise: Different Handgrips, Different Synergy.” Sports, 2023. • Marcolin G. et al. “Differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl.” PeerJ, 2018. The Pallof press builds real core stability… not just abs. It trains your body to resist rotation… which is exactly what protects your lower back when you lift, twist, or move in real life. If your back feels vulnerable… this is where you start. #pallofpress #corestability  #backpainrelief #corestrength  #functionalstrength

Replying to @lisam3332 Grip strength training for over 50… how to improve grip strength fast using dead hangs and loaded carries. Weak grip is one of the first signs of strength loss with age… but it comes back quickly with simple daily work. Build stronger hands, forearms and real world strength with these basic movements. #gripstrength #over50 #stronghands #forearmtraining #functionalstrength

Grip strength test over 50… can you hang for 30 seconds? This simple dead hang test is strongly linked to overall strength, health, and longevity. If your grip is weak… everything else follows. Try it today and see where you stand.  #gripstrength #over50  #deadhang #strengthtest #healthyaging

Legs aching after lunges is usually a normal response to new load, especially if you haven’t used that position for years. Front of thigh soreness means your quads are being challenged… not damaged. Support at the start is fine… progress comes quickly with consistency. l#lunges #legstrength #over50  #kneepain  #strengthtraining

Bone density after 50 isn’t built with calcium alone. Impact training like small daily jumps sends a mechanical signal through your skeleton that helps maintain bone strength. No impact means no signal and bones weaken over time. Strong bones need load not protection. #bonedensity #strongbones  #impacttraining #over50fitness #agingstrong

Strong legs support everyday movement, independence and quality of life. They carry you upstairs, get you out of chairs and keep you capable as you age. Here’s a quick leg strength test. Ten squats. Ten walking lunges each leg. Finish with a thirty-second wall sit. Simple movements… but they tell you a lot about your leg strength, balance and endurance. legstrength  #stronglegs #longevity #mobility #fitness

Squats are one of the best exercises for building strong legs, but many people avoid them because of knee pain. A suspension trainer lets you take weight off your legs while you relearn proper squat movement. You can start by lowering yourself to a chair, control the descent, and let your knees track naturally again. Over time reduce the assistance and rebuild your squat strength safely. squat  #legtraining  #stronglegs #kneepain  #trx

Deep squat problems often come from restricted ankle mobility. If your heels lift or you can’t reach an Asian squat / deep squat, your ankles may not allow the knee to travel forward. These three drills help improve ankle mobility, calf flexibility and squat depth so your hips, knees and ankles can work together. Work on ankle flexibility first… the squat becomes much easier. #anklemobility #deepsquat #asiansquat #flexibility #mobility

Deep squat (often called the Asian squat) builds ankle mobility, hip flexibility and leg strength. If you can’t sit comfortably in a deep squat yet, start from a low seat and let your hips, knees and ankles adapt. A suspension trainer can give you support while you control the descent and stand back up. This is how you rebuild squat mobility safely and regain the deep squat position used in yoga, flexibility and leg training. Tap the bag if you want the suspension trainer. #asiansquat  #deepsquat  #mobility  #flexibility  #legtraining

Creatine monohydrate is one of the most researched supplements for maintaining strength and muscle. After 50, muscle mass and power decline faster, which is why strength training and proper supplementation can matter more. Creatine helps support strength, training performance and lean muscle when combined with resistance training. This one is micronised, so it mixes easily and there’s no loading phase needed. Just 3–5 grams a day. #creatine #creatinemonohydrate #strengthtraining  #after50  #supplements

If you’ve been told to strengthen your core to “Fix” your lower back pain, I’m sorry, try this instead…. While core strength can help improve the health of your lower back, it’s not the only solution to lower back pain, stiffness, tension or chronic aches. There are 4 major areas that play a role in the health of your lower back 1. Breathing 2. Spine 3. Hips 4. Core Start with focusing on your breathing mechanics and functionality. When we’re using our breath to it’s fullest natural capacity then we offload pressure, reduce stress, and load down into the lumbar spine. This allows our internal support system of the diaphragm, pelvic floor, TA and multifidi to function as they were meant to, supporting you from inside. In our live class this morning,  “Form/less” you’ll move from structured segments of Pilates and movement sequences into guided free formless time to explore and release your body.  Our body loves to live in the spaces between form and formlessness…. One of the very first elements of movement you’ll learn on Modern Body is form. Knowing our form form function of your body including alignment, joints mechanics, posture, placement, what muscles are working etc. is extremely important. It’s like learning the letters of the alphabet before you begin to read or write. But once we’ve gained our understanding of form then we can allow ourselves to release that form. Knowing when the time to call on your form and let go of form is one of the most underrated aspects of understanding our body.  We often get so caught up in doing everything perfectly, that we forget that our body wants to be free to move however it needs to.  After all, whats the point of training our body if we can’t allow it to move as it was meant to.

Cardio is not the enemy in this story…. Many of use have been taught that cardio is purely to burn calories and lose weight, but what if there was a different side to the story? Is your movement supporting your pelvic floor health? The pelvic floor is one of those areas that doesn’t get much love until something goes wrong, but that doesn’t have to be true for you.  You can prime, prepare, and support your pelvic floor throughout your week by making sure you’re getting these 3 elements into your movement 1. Breathing 2. Mobility 3. Strength + Stability  Breathing is one of the most underrated aspects of pelvic floor health. We can strengthen and lengthen our pelvic floor simply by breathing to get the diaphragm and pelvic floor in sync with one another. (Kegel not required) Make sure to have the head, ribs, and pelvis all vertically stacked on top of each other while working on this. Breathing into your diaphragm, letting your abdomen slightly expand and lightly lifting the pelvic floor away from floor. We want to be able to both let the pelvic floor relax and expand as we inhale and gently activate and respond to efforts as we exhale.  Mobility of both the femur on a stable pelvis and the pelvis on a stable femur in all directions will help bring movement to the pelvic floor. Thoracic mobility is also need because just like in breathing if the diaphragm can’t move, neither can the pelvic floor and they both want to move.  Strength + Stability in all planes of motion, all direction, and all positions from the floor to kneeling to standing. We want to build strength throughout the hip joint so the Pelvic floor is supported and not taking on all the load and work all the time.  If you want to support the health of your pelvic floor sustainably and consciously every single class on Modern Body will help you. Each of our classes are designed to support your body from inside to outside starting with breathing and moving outward.  you can start classes on Modern Body today with a 7-day free trial and begin to improve the health of your pelvic floor one day at a time. leave the word MODERN in the comments below and I’ll send you the link to get started to your inbox.

It’s not just about doing MORE ab work. Yes, abs can be developed and strengthened through targeted core training. But, they won’t be visible if you have visceral and subcutaneous fat that’s covering it. Visceral fat is the deep “hidden” fat surrounding your organs (the most dangerous type of at that leads to major health issues). Subcutaneous fat is the fat directly underneath the surface of your skin, the type of fat that you can pinch.  So while you can do all of the crunches in the world, if you don’t cut through the fat that’s covering your muscles, you won’t get results that you can actually see in the mirror. #weightlosstips #fitover30 #healthyweightlosstips #Weightlosstip #fitnesstipsforwomen

You’ll be shocked to find out⤵ The most obvious forms of sugar are in your traditional cookies, donuts, candy, ice cream, etc. But the not so obvious are lurking in your ketchup, salad dressings, cereal, BBQ sauce, low fat yogurt, and even spaghetti sauce. It can be in your premade soup, your protein bars, even in your sushi rice! If you’re trying to reduce your overall sugar intake, it’s important to know that there are literally over 73 different names for sugar. And if you don’t know what you should be looking for on ingredient labels, you might think you’re eating a health food when it’s really not! #weightlosstips #fitover30 #healthyweightlosstips #Weightlosstip #fitnesstipsforwomen

Struggling with a stubborn belly pooch? Here’s the fix ⤵ I see so many women carrying weight particularly in their midsection for a few different reasons. But one mistake (that can EASILY be fixed) is eating in a STRESSED environment. Here’s what I mean: ❌ You’re inhaling your food down without properly chewing it down ❌ You’re eating a protein bar as your hurriedly get to your next appointment ❌ You’re finishing up your huge plate of dinner in less than 8 minutes to get the little ones to bed You might even be eating all the “right foods,” but the WAY you’re eating it can cause poor digestion, less nutrient uptake, bloating, and of course, may lead to extra belly fat. Don’t believe me? One of my clients carried all of her excess fat in her midsection. As soon as she made food the PRIMARY event (no distractions) and slowed TF down, she started to lose inches in her waist. Not because she changed what she was eating. Simply because she changed HOW she was eating. When you eat in a CALM state (aka chew your food slowly, take your time, and make food the PRIMARY event in your day), you’re able to digest your food better. Satiety increases. You feel fuller off of less food. All of this contributes to better nutrient absorption, less bloating, and less fat in your midsection. #weightlosstips #fitover30 #healthyweightlosstips #Weightlosstip #fitnesstipsforwomen

Your diaphragm is a core muscle, and your breathing mechanics are probably wrong. Following on from the transversus abdominis we covered in my last post, let me show you something most people miss: the diaphragm is the roof of your core system. When you breathe properly, your diaphragm moves down, it increases intra-abdominal pressure, and that pressure stabilizes your spine. That’s not a side effect — that’s the whole point. But most people chest breathe. All movement, no pressure. Their diaphragm doesn’t create stability, so their transversus has to work overtime, and everything else compensates. Fix the breathing, and suddenly the whole core system works better. This is the missing link in core training that nobody talks about. Next post we’re going inside the spinal stabilizers — multifidus. If you think your bad posture is slowly destroying your spine… listen carefully. Because posture is being blamed for pain it doesn’t actually cause. And anterior pelvic tilt? It’s the favorite villain. But here’s what no one tells you 👇 Anterior pelvic tilt is simply the angle between two points: 📍 ASIS in the front 📍 PSIS in the back If you haven’t palpated those landmarks yourself, you don’t actually know your tilt angle. Some people naturally sit in more anterior tilt. Others are more neutral. That’s structural variability — not dysfunction. And 10–15 degrees of anterior tilt does not automatically compress discs or create back pain. Here’s the truth: Pain is about load tolerance, motor control, and tissue capacity — not just static angles in a mirror. Now, if you still want to improve pelvic control, here’s where to start: ✔️ Load posterior tilt using bands ✔️ Train glutes with glute bridges — emphasizing posterior tilt ✔️ Strengthen the psoas in a lengthened position That’s how you build resilience. Not fear. If you’re still blaming posture for your pain, comment “POSTURE” and I’ll send you my free assessment guide. #PostureMyths #AnteriorPelvicTilt #LowBackPain #SpineHealth #OMNIMethod 🔗 www.omniprehab.com

Struggling with shallow breathing when you’re stressed? This muscle might be part of it. Meet the psoas major. You know it as a hip flexor. But here’s what most people miss 👇 It connects directly to the diaphragm through the medial arcuate ligament. And the diaphragm is controlled by the phrenic nerve — the nerve that drives your breathing. So think about that. If the psoas is tight or overactive… It can influence how your diaphragm moves. And if your breathing is stress-driven and shallow… That tension feeds right back into the psoas. It’s a loop. Breathing → spine → tension → back to breathing. So if you’re constantly tight, stressed, or stuck in rib-dominant breathing… Stretching your hips alone won’t fix it. You have to address the system. 👇 Comment “PSOAS MAJOR” and I’ll send you the assessment guide. 🎓 Clinicians — deeper breakdowns at www.omniprehab.com #psoasmajor #breathingmechanics #movementscience #sportsrehab #functionaltraining

Most women in peri-menopause and menopause are never taught how to exercise correctly for the female body. That's why I focus at this time of year, I help women with my Perimenopause Body or Menopause Body Systems. These are three of my favourite simple exercises on the floor for tightening the tummy, pinching the waist and helping reduce menopause belly fat. I'm 60 and happier with my body now than I was in my 40's! No complicated gym routines. No endless cardio. Just intelligent movement you can do lying on your back at home. Just put a towel down on the floor in front of the news. We can even do them in your bed before you get out a bit in the morning if you want to! Couldn't be simpler. 1. Windscreen wipers Keep your spine pressed into the mat, arms out wide and slowly lower the legs from side to side with control. 2. Around the world Tiny gap between the feet and slowly circle the legs all the way around in one direction for 10 repetitions, then the other, keeping the lower back connected to the mat. Slow and controlled is everything. 3. Dead bugs Legs perpendicular. Opposite arm and leg extend away, then return together before switching sides. Brilliant for deep core control and waist tightening. Do 10 reps of each exercise and repeat the circuit 3 times. Aim for 3-4 times per week, and you will genuinely start to notice a flatter tummy and tighter waistline. If muscle-ups are a goal, you should consider building a strong false grip 💪💪💪  False grip is advantageous for many as your wrists are sitting on top of the bar, so you can move from the pull to push in one fluid motion without releasing your hands from the bar.  ✅ I prefer using more of a hybrid false grip and have the bar sitting on the base of my wrists, and wrap my fingers and thumbs around the bar.  ✅ This grip allows for a very strong pull, and removes most if not all of the discomfort people experience when using a false grip.  ❌ Some people sit the bar on the base of their wrists but don’t wrap their fingers around the bar (pure false grip).  ❌ I am not a fan of this grip as the bar is pressing against your wrists SO hard and I find bruises and chafes the skin. Your wrists are basically supporting all of your bodyweight, and it doesn’t feel good!  ❌ Without the fingers and thumbs around the bar, the pull is usually much weaker and it’s much tougher to control what your elbows are doing.  👉👉 If you are new to learning false grip, start off doing:  1️⃣ False grip hangs  Once this feels good, progress to doing:  2️⃣ False grip pull-ups  3️⃣ Hanging in the top positon of the pull-up using a false grip  4️⃣ Eccentric muscle-ups  5️⃣ Banded muscle-ups  If the first 4 exercises feel too tough you can modify by keeping your feet on the floor like you’d do with inverted rows. What does a week of my training look like?  As I am asked this question a lot, I decided to make a video of what my training looks like.  This video is obviously just a small jumbled sample of what I do. I wish I had been training this way in my 20s and 30s! At 45, I feel better than ever, I love my training more than ever, and I’m grateful for how much excitement and joy my training brings me. I absolutely love to coach, and I love to train! I hope some of my passion rubs off on the people I work with and people who follow me. Being able to train and feel good truly as a gift, and is something I will never take for granted again! In terms of my training, I typically do:  Workout 1: Calisthenics focused workout (largely muscle-ups, weighted pull-ups/chin-ups, push-ups, inverted rows, and some accessory work. Monday EAT fit meal! When it comes to soup recipes, I LOVE a classic Leek and Potato Soup. It's simple and delicious. Leeks are highly nutritious allium vegetable  that offer significant benefits for your heart, gut, and immune system while being exceptionally low in calories. Part of the same botanical family as garlic and onions, they feature a much milder, sweeter flavor profile while packing a dense concentration of protective antioxidants, vitamins, and minerals. Leeks are an excellent source of prebiotic fiber, specifically inulin. This fiber feeds and nourishes the beneficial bacteria in your microbiome, optimizing digestion and reducing bloating. They contain the flavonoid kaempferol, which helps safeguard blood vessel linings. They also provide potassium to help regulate blood pressure and folate to prevent compound buildups linked to heart disease.  If you’re lucky enough you can forage your own leeks this time of year.  Most Potato & Leek soup recipes use flour as thickening agent- this recipe contains no flour.  Ingredients  4 cups chopped potatoes  2 cups chopped leeks  2 cups choice of milk  2 tablespoons butter  1 tsp celery salt  1 tsp black pepper  1 tablespoon ginger powder  Directions  Boil 3 cups potatoes & remove skin after boiling. Remove water & let potatoes sit.  Sauté 2 cups chopped leeks in 2 tablespoons of butter until softened & browned.  Mash potatoes with hand stick blender in same pot used for boiled. Once mashed add in and blend leeks and milk & spices. (If you like your soup less thick..add more milk to consistency you like).  Warm it up on stove top & serve! Looking for a healthier cookie with less sugar and more protein and fibre than most?  These peanut butter chocolate chip cookies are higher protein, sweetened with banana and no sugar! Added sweetener is optional! Since there are no eggs in this recipe - taste before you bake! Add more sweetener as needed. This recipe works with chick pea or red or white kidney beans.  Here’s the recipe - I bet no one will guess that  these cookies are made with beans!  * 1 x 15oz or 540ml can chickpeas or white or red kidney beans or navy beans rinsed and drained * 1 ripe banana  * ½ cup nut butter  * ⅓ cup powder sweetener (I used stevia)  * 2 teaspoons vanilla * ½ teaspoon baking soda * ½ teaspoon baking powder * ½ teaspoon salt & 1/2 - 1 cup stevia chocolate chips  Blend the beans so they are super smooth! It should look just like  cookie dough! Mix in all the other ingredients saving chocolate chips for the end and feel free to taste as you go! Add more sweetener if you think you need it.  You can drop these cookies by teaspoon or roll into balks & press flat with fork so they make a nice round cookie shape. Bake 350 for 15 minutes! Enjoy! They store well in freezer until needed. Let’s look at the way we Climb stairs! Are you tip toeing or heel stomping?  1. Tip-Toe Stair Climbing  When you climb stairs strictly on the balls of your feet, your heels never touch the surface. Forcing your body up via the toes turns your ankles and calves into springs, which builds localized endurance in the lower legs (calves).  Leaning forward shifts your center of gravity, causing your knees to track far over your toes and placing higher shear stress on the knee joints. It eliminates the impact of the heel, making it the preferred method for moving silently through a quiet house.  Consistently preferring to tip-toe up stairs can sometimes be a sign of tight Achilles tendons or just habit.  Heel-Stomp Stair Climbing When you place your entire foot flatly onto a step and push downward through the heel, you maximize your structural frame. Driving through the heel recruits the large muscles of your buttocks and hamstrings, providing more raw power for vertical lifting. The intentional weight-bearing impact (the "stomp") signals your skeletal system to stimulate bone growth and density, which helps slow down bone loss!  Stacking your weight directly over a flat foot protects the cartilage of the knee, making it highly recommended by experts for painful or arthritic joints. Pushing straight down with massive force transfers vibration directly into the floor structure, generating loud footsteps.  For daily biomechanical efficiency and long-term joint health, flat-foot climbing with heel drive is the superior movement pattern.#stairs #heels #toes #rosaliebrown

Iodine Your Hormone Hero Iodine: The Unsung Thyroid Mineral Iodine plays a key role in the production of thyroid hormones. Your thyroid produces: 🔹 T4 (contains 4 iodine atoms) 🔹 T3 (contains 3 iodine atoms) And here’s the key point: Your body cannot produce iodine on its own — you must get it from your diet. Common sources include: 🌊 Seaweed 🥛 Dairy products 🥚 Eggs Adequate iodine intake supports normal thyroid function and overall hormonal balance. Small mineral. Big role. ✨ #Iodine #ThyroidSupport #HormoneHealth #Micronutrients #WellnessBasics #health

Electrolytes: The Body’s Messengers They’re not just for sports drinks. 👀 Electrolytes are charged minerals that help your body communicate. Somewhere along the way, so many women were taught that life was over after a certain age. That their dreams no longer mattered. That their bodies were supposed to be hidden. That adventure belonged to the young. That peace was something they had to earn after suffering. I reject that completely. I believe women deserve to feel beautiful, vibrant, sensual, healthy, adventurous, soft, confident, and free at every stage of life. And if you’ve been feeling restless lately… emotionally heavy… unfulfilled… or like there has to be more for you than simply surviving… maybe your spirit is trying to wake you back up. This next season of my life is not about perfection. It is about reclamation. Reclaiming our bodies. Reclaiming our confidence. Reclaiming our health. Reclaiming our peace. Reclaiming our time. Reclaiming ourselves. And if that speaks to something deep inside of you… then beauty, maybe it’s time to join me. ✨ Comment “RECLAIM” if you are ready for your next chapter. #BodyReclamation #WomenOver40 #MoTheGoddess

You cannot starve your way into a healthy body, beauties. One of the biggest mistakes people make on a fitness journey is skipping breakfast, thinking they’re “saving calories,” when in reality they’re slowing down their metabolism, spiking stress hormones, and setting themselves up to binge later. Your body needs fuel. Your body needs nourishment. Your body needs consistency. This morning was simple but intentional… healthy oatmeal, fruit, and eggs prepared with love because reclaiming your body starts with the rituals you commit to daily. Not punishment. Not extremes. Rituals. Inside the 40-Day Body Reclamation Program, we are learning how to reconnect with our bodies again through nourishment, movement, nervous system healing, de-bloating practices, discipline, and self-respect. Mind, body, and spirit. Because the goal is not just weight loss… it’s transformation. And trust me… when you start feeding your body like it matters, everything begins to shift. #BodyReclamation #EatBeautyLiveBeautiful #WellnessJourney

Everybody wants access to a woman like this… until they realize she comes with standards, discipline, depth, boundaries, and a price for her energy. You thought the body was the power. No, beauties… the power is the woman inside the body who finally understands her worth. I’m no longer interested in being consumed for free. Not my energy. Not my softness. Not my presence. Not my time. Some of you call it confidence. Some of you call it intimidation. Some of you call it goddess energy. I call it finally remembering who I am. And the moment a woman truly understands her value, the entire room shifts around her. The gaze changes. The treatment changes. The opportunities change. The offerings change. As they should. #MoTheGoddess #FemininePower #SensualSovereignty

I can’t lie… I’ve been feeling sorry for myself. I’ve been making excuses. And before anybody says it, yes, the pain has been real. My back has been absolutely killing me. The nerve pain has been relentless, and combined with this knee injury, there were days where I felt completely crippled. But if I’m being honest, I started watching myself slowly disappear into it. Month after month… more weight, less movement, less confidence, more frustration. And eventually I had to sit myself down and ask: “Are you going to keep sitting here feeling sorry for yourself year after year… or are you going to find a way?” Because the truth is, the body still needs movement. Even in pain. Even in discomfort. Even when you can’t go hard like you used to. So I started doing chair exercises. No, it’s not some intense cardio session. No, I’m not flipping tires or lifting heavy weights. But it is something. It is movement. It is effort. It is me refusing to completely give up on myself. And sometimes healing starts there. Not with perfection. Not with beast mode. Just with consistency. Small choices. Better food. Daily movement. A decision to stop abandoning yourself. This season of my life is teaching me that you don’t need to do the most… you just need to keep going. And that’s exactly what I plan to do.

One thing about me… I am going to choose the life that feels aligned over the life that simply looks acceptable to society. That decision has cost me comfort, certainty, and sometimes even understanding from other people. But it has also given me something priceless: freedom. Freedom to create. Freedom to evolve. Freedom to wake up and actually feel connected to the woman I see in the mirror. I think deep down, a lot of people know they were meant for more… but fear, conditioning, and survival mode keep them living the same day over and over again. And I refuse to get to the end of my life carrying untouched dreams, buried desires, and unexplored parts of myself. You do not need permission to become who you were always meant to be.  @thegodbodyrituals  #ThePowerMethod #FreedomLifestyle #MoTheGoddess

Being thick is one thing. Being thick, toned, sculpted, and built like a whole brick house? That hits different. And let me be honest… my body is naturally prone to holding weight. My lower half carries everything first — glutes, thighs, stomach, water retention, inflammation, all of it. So I don’t have the luxury of neglecting myself and expecting magic. I have to WORK with my body. I have to stay intentional. I have to move even when I don’t feel like it. Right now I’m training with 5-pound ankle weights, doing 20 reps per leg for 4 sets before moving into other exercises. I’m also realizing how much I neglected stretching and mobility, and baby… your body will humble you when you ignore the maintenance. Do I hurt? Absolutely. My back hurts. My knee hurts. Some days I’m exhausted. But it’s a catch-22 because neglect only makes it worse. Weakness grows where discipline disappears. And I refuse to sit back and watch my body deteriorate when I still have the power to strengthen it. This season is not about perfection. It’s about preservation. It’s about staying strong enough to carry the woman I’m becoming. #GodBodByMo #BodyReclamation #EatBeautyLiveBeautiful

My Oreo and milky stars cheesecake.  500g digestive biscuit crushed.  150g melted butter. 600g soft cheese. 100g icing sugar. 284ml double cream. 1 tbs vanilla extract.  Plenty of Oreo’s and milky stars. Mix butter and biscuits until biscuit is completely covered. Leave in fridge for 1 hour. Whisk double cream until it thickens. In separate bowl mix the soft cheese, icing sugar and vanilla extract until smooth and thickening. Add the double cream and crushed Oreo biscuits and fold in. Add to biscuit base and leave in fridge for 2-3hours. Add Oreo and milky stars topping and put back in the fridge over night. LINK IN BIO✨✨ 📌Big backs happen for different reasons, the most common being having a high body fat percentage. You MUST lose body fat FIRST to see any back definition, and the only way to do that is to be in a CALORIC DEFICIT. The best way to get into a caloric deficit is to eat 500 cal under your maintenance calories AND perform at least 20-30 minutes of either low or medium intensity cardio 3-5 times a week. 📌The other reason that your back might be proportionally bigger (in comparison to the rest of your body) is that you might have the WRONG RATIO of upper body exercises (focusing more on shoulders/lats—like lat pulldowns or pull ups) OR lifting fairly heavy on upper body day (which is not necessarily a negative thing in and of itself.. but may not be consistent with the goal of building a defined, feminine back without making it wider/bigger). 📌To build a sexy, feminine, and defined back, focus on the middle traps, lower traps, rhomboids, and posterior delts). The exercises in this vid are some of my fav for this purpose. Plus you can feed yourself and the kiddies at the same time with minimal effort, which makes everyone happy.  I know It's that "New Year New  Me" season and everybody's resolutions are flying left and right. But I promise you sis, you'll fall off that wagon every single time if you don't have a sustainable system that stands the test of your busy life. So, Eat less calories with more fiber and prioritize your protein, which will help you lose the fat and keep that azz--and if you combine that with working out CONSISTENTLY 3 times a week, won't nobody be able to tell you NOTHING this summer, OKKKK! So, that's the blueprint, girlie.  And, if you need a little nudge in the right direction, I gotchu boo, just head to the link in my bio!  Soup Ingredients 8 medium tomatoes 1 yellow onion 2 garlic cloves 1 red bell pepper 1 tbsp olive oil garlic powder, onion powder, cajon seasoning of your choice, salt and pepper to taste 2 cups bone broth 1/4 cup half and half handful basil leaves Grilled Cheese 2 slices sourdough low fat mayo 1/2 cup sharp cheddar (for flavor) and mozzarella cheese (for pull) Preheat oven to 400F Chop Veggies, add seasoning, roast in oven for 30-40 min Add veggies and bone broth to blender and blend till smooth Bring soup to boil in a medium pan (medium heat) and add half and half and chopped basil to the soup Let the soup simmer x 10 minutes til thick While soup is simmering, coat the outside of sourdough with light mayo Place mayo side of bread down on the pan and then top with cheese. Top off the sandwich with the other side of sourdough (mayo side facing up) The key is to brown the sandwich with low to medium heat on both sides So flip the sandwich when the bread is light brown and cheese melts. Ini contoh rutinitas 30 menit yang bisa kamu jalanin 4x seminggu: 1. *Rutinitas Full Body 30 Menit - Tanpa Alat* Lakuin berurutan, istirahat 30 detik antar gerakan. 3 ronde total. *Pemanasan 4 menit* - Jumping jack / march di tempat 1 menit - Arm circles 30 detik - Bodyweight squat 1 menit - Dynamic stretch pinggul & bahu 1 menit *Blok Kekuatan 15 menit* 1. *Squat* 15x – paha, bokong, core 2. *Push-up / Wall Push-up* 10-15x – dada, lengan, bahu   3. *Glute Bridge* 15x – bokong, paha belakang, punggung bawah 4. *Bent Over Row pakai band* 12x – punggung, lengan 5. *Plank* 30-45 detik – core keseluruhan *Blok Kardio + Core 8 menit*   HIIT style: 40 detik kerja, 20 detik istirahat 1. Mountain climbers 2. Standing knee to elbow 3. High knees 4. Side plank kanan-kiri 20 detik tiap sisi *Pendinginan 3 menit* Stretching paha, hamstring, bahu, punggung. Bantu recovery dan kurangi pegal. 2. *Tips Biar Nggak Bosan & Tetap Progres* 1. *Naikin kesulitan tiap minggu*: Tambah repetisi 2-3x, atau tahan plank lebih lama 5 detik. 2. *Pakai resistance band*: Kaitkan di paha pas squat, atau di tangan pas row. Instan lebih berat. 3. *Fokus form dulu*: 10 squat bener lebih bagus dari 20 squat asal. Cegah cedera. 4. *Catat progress*: Tulis berapa repetisi & waktu plank. Lihat angka naik = motivasi naik. 3. *Jadwal Mingguan yang Realistis* - *Senin*: Full body workout di atas - *Selasa*: Jalan cepat 30 menit + stretching - *Rabu*: Full body workout - *Kamis*: Rest / yoga 15 menit - *Jumat*: Full body workout   - *Sabtu*: Kardio santai 40 menit - sepeda, jalan incline - *Minggu*: Rest total 4. *Kesalahan Umum yang Bikin Nggak Ada Hasil* 1. *Cuma cardio, skip strength*: Otot kempes, metabolisme turun. Strength yang bikin badan kenceng. 2. *Makan sembarangan*: Olahraga bakar 300 kkal, tapi 1 boba 400 kkal. Defisit kalori tetap kunci buat turun lemak. 3. *Kurang tidur*: Tidur <6 jam bikin hormon lapar naik dan recovery lambat. 4. *Mau instan*: Perubahan nyata keliatan di minggu 4-6 kalau konsisten. 5. *Mana yang Dipilih Kalau Waktu Mepek* Nggak ada 30 menit? Lakuin *10 menit EMOM*:   Set timer 10 menit. Tiap menit lakuin 10 squat + 5 push-up + 20 detik plank. Sisanya istirahat.   Lebih baik 10 menit konsisten daripada 0 menit. #creatorsearchinsights *Pilates at home* is perfect because you only need a mat and your bodyweight. It’s low impact, so it’s great for core strength, posture, flexibility, and tightening without bulking up. Here’s a no-equipment routine you can start today. 1. *The 20-Minute Full Body Pilates Flow* Do this 3-4x per week. Move slow, control the movement, breathe. That’s where the “burn” comes from. *Warm-up 3 min* 1. *Cat-Cow*: 8 reps. Loosens spine, wakes up core. 2. *Spine Twist*: Sitting, rotate side to side 10 reps. Mobilizes lower back. *Core & Abs 7 min* 1. *The Hundred*: 100 pulses. Lie on back, legs up, pump arms. Hits deep core. If too hard, keep feet down. 2. *Single Leg Stretch*: 10 reps each side. Flat abs, zero neck strain. 3. *Criss Cross*: 10 reps each side. Obliques and waist. *Legs & Glutes 6 min* 1. *Glute Bridge*: 15 reps. Lift hips slow, squeeze at top. 2. *Clamshells*: 15 reps each side. Lying on side, open knees. Tightens outer thighs and hips. 3. *Leg Circles*: 8 circles each leg, both directions. Hip mobility + core stability. *Upper Body & Stretch 4 min* 1. *Swan Dive Prep*: 8 reps. Lie face down, lift chest. Opens chest, strengthens back. 2. *Child’s Pose*: 1 min. Release lower back. 3. *Seated Spine Stretch*: 1 min. Lengthen hamstrings and spine. 2. *Why Pilates Works for Tightening* 1. *It targets deep core muscles*: Transverse abdominis, pelvic floor. That’s what gives you a flat, pulled-in look, not just a 6-pack. 2. *Improves posture*: Most “belly pooch” and loose upper body comes from anterior pelvic tilt and rounded shoulders. Pilates fixes it. 3. *Low impact, high control*: You won’t strain joints, but you’ll shake from muscle fatigue. That’s the good burn. 3. *Common Mistakes to Avoid* 1. *Using momentum*: If you’re swinging, you’re not doing Pilates. Every move should be slow and controlled. 2. *Holding breath*: Exhale on the effort, inhale on the release. Breath drives the core engagement. 3. *Neck straining*: If your neck hurts in crunches, you’re pulling with your neck. Eyes stay on belly, chin slightly tucked. 4. *Skipping glutes and back*: A strong back and glutes make the whole core work better. 4. *Equipment That Levels It Up - Optional* You don’t need it, but these make it more fun: - *Resistance band*: Adds tension to leg and arm work. - *Pilates ball*: 20cm ball between thighs or under lower back for extra core challenge. - *Mat with grip*: Stops slipping during leg circles. 5. *What to Expect* - *Week 1-2*: Core feels sore in a good way. Posture starts improving. - *Week 3-4*: Stomach feels flatter, back pain reduces, you stand taller. - *Week 6+*: Visible toning in abs, arms, thighs if you’re also in a slight calorie deficit. *Pro tip*: Quality > reps. 8 perfect reps beat 20 sloppy ones. If you feel it in your neck or lower back, stop and check form. Want me to give you a 4-week progression plan so you don’t plateau and keep seeing results at home? #pejuangsehat #olahragasehat #pilates

#creatorsearchinsights  *Olahraga untuk bahu* itu tujuannya 3: bikin bahu lebih tegak, ngilangin bungkuk, dan ngencengin area lengan atas biar nggak kendur. Bahu juga sering tegang kalau kerja di laptop seharian. Kamu bisa lakuin semua ini di rumah pakai resistance band panjang atau tanpa alat. 1. *Gerakan Wajib Buat Bahu Kuat & Rapi* Lakuin 3 set, 12-15 repetisi. Istirahat 30 detik antar set. 1. *Banded Shoulder Press*      Injak band, pegang ujungnya di bahu. Dorong ke atas lurus.      _Fungsi_: Bahu depan + samping. Bikin bahu keliatan lebih bidang. 2. *Banded Face Pull*      Kaitkan band di tiang setinggi dada. Tarik ke arah wajah, siku buka lebar.      _Fungsi_: Bahu belakang + punggung atas. Obat paling ampuh buat bungkuk. 3. *Lateral Raise Tanpa Beban*      Angkat tangan ke samping sampai sejajar bahu, turun pelan 3 detik.      _Fungsi_: Bentuk bahu samping biar nggak rata. Pakai botol air 1L kalau mau ditambah beban. 4. *Wall Angels*      Tempel punggung ke tembok, tangan bentuk “W” lalu geser ke atas jadi “Y”.      _Fungsi_: Perbaiki postur dan buka otot dada yang ketarik ke depan. 5. *Arm Circles*      Putar tangan kecil ke depan 15x, lalu ke belakang 15x.      _Fungsi_: Pemanasan + melancarkan peredaran darah di bahu. 2. *Rutinitas 15 Menit Buat Pemula* Cocok kalau kamu kerja duduk seharian dan bahu sering pegal. *Senin & Kamis:* 1. Wall Angels 2 menit 2. Banded Face Pull 3x15 3. Lateral Raise 3x15 4. Arm Circles 2 menit *Rabu & Sabtu:* 1. Banded Shoulder Press 3x12 2. Push-up Dinding 3x15 3. Shoulder Shrug dengan band 3x15 4. Stretching bahu 3 menit Hari lain jalan kaki 20 menit biar sirkulasi lancar. 3. *Kesalahan yang Bikin Bahu Malah Sakit* 1. *Ngangkat bahu saat latihan*: Pas angkat tangan, turunin bahu dulu. Jangan sampai naik ke telinga. 2. *Gerakan terlalu cepat*: Bahu itu sendi rapuh. Turunkan beban pelan 3 detik. 3. *Skip pemanasan*: Bahu gampang keseleo. Lakuin arm circles 2 menit sebelum mulai. 4. *Cuma fokus depan*: Kebanyakan orang cuma latihan bahu depan. Akibatnya bungkuk. Imbangin dengan face pull dan row. 4. *Tips Biar Bahu Cepat Rapi* 1. *Perbaiki posisi duduk*: Layar sejajar mata, siku 90 derajat. Postur buruk = bahu tegang terus. 2. *Stretching tiap 1 jam kerja*: Angkat tangan ke atas, tarik ke belakang 20 detik. Simple tapi ngaruh. 3. *Tidur miring salah*: Hindari tidur miring dengan tangan di bawah kepala. Bikin bahu kejepit. 4. *Kompres hangat kalau pegal*: 10 menit sebelum tidur buat lepasin otot yang tegang. 5. *Hasilnya Kapan Keliatan* - *Minggu 1-2*: Bahu nggak gampang pegal, postur lebih tegak. - *Minggu 3-4*: Bahu keliatan lebih kenceng, baju lebih pas di bahu. - *Minggu 6+*: Perubahan postur permanen kalau konsisten. Kalau kamu punya riwayat cedera bahu atau nyeri tajam saat angkat tangan, stop dan cek dokter dulu ya. #creatorsearchinsights *Paha ramping* itu kombinasi 3 hal: nurunin lemak di paha, ngencengin otot, dan ngurangin retensi air. Nggak bisa cuma olahraga aja tanpa jaga makan, dan nggak bisa cuma diet tanpa gerak. Ini yang bener-bener ngaruh: 1. *Latihan yang Bikin Paha Kenceng, Bukan Tambah Besar* Fokus ke repetisi tinggi, beban ringan-sedang, gerakan kontrol. Hindari angkat beban berat kalau tujuannya ramping, bukan nambah massa otot. *Rutinitas 20 menit, 4x seminggu:* 1. *Sumo Squat* 3x15      Kaki lebar, ujung kaki keluar 45°. Fokus ke paha dalam. Ini area paling susah kenceng. 2. *Lunge Berjalan* 3x12 tiap kaki      Jalan maju sambil lunge. Bakar paha depan + belakang + bokong. 3. *Side Leg Raise* 3x20 tiap sisi      Tidur miring, angkat kaki atas pelan. Bentuk paha luar biar nggak “gebyar”. 4. *Wall Sit* 3x40-60 detik      Punggung nempel tembok, posisi duduk. Rasain paha kebakar. Ningkatin daya tahan otot. 5. *Glute Bridge Satu Kaki* 3x12 tiap kaki      Tidur telentang, angkat satu kaki lurus. Fokus ke paha belakang & bokong. Pakai resistance band panjang di paha buat bikin lebih berat kalau udah gampang. 2. *Kardio yang Nggak Bikin Paha Tambah Besar* Hindari sprint dan lari cepat jarak pendek kalau takut paha tambah berot. Pilih: 1. *Jalan cepat incline 5-10%* 30-40 menit, 3x seminggu. Bakar lemak tanpa bikin otot besar. 2. *Bersepeda santai* atau elliptical. Low impact, aman buat lutut. 3. *Skipping pelan* 5 menit diselingi istirahat. Bagus buat bakar kalori. 3. *Makan yang Bikin Paha Nggak Gampang Bengkak* Paha sering keliatan besar karena lemak + air + bengkak. 1. *Kurangi garam & makanan olahan*: Garam bikin retensi air. Paha keliatan lebih besar. 2. *Protein cukup*: 1.6g per kg berat badan. Bantu jaga otot biar paha kenceng waktu lemak turun. 3. *Air putih 2-2.5L sehari*: Kebalikan dari mitos. Kurang minum = tubuh nahan air. 4. *Kurangi gula & gorengan*: Inflamasi bikin paha gampang bengkak dan selulit lebih keliatan. 4. *Kesalahan yang Bikin Paha Nggak Ramping-Ramping* 1. *Cuma fokus squat berat*: Otot paha depan jadi besar. Kalau tujuannya ramping, prioritaskan lunge, side raise, wall sit. 2. *Nggak konsisten kardio*: Latihan beban aja nggak cukup buat bakar lemak paha. 3. *Kurang tidur*: Kurang tidur 6 jam = hormon lapar naik, lemak susah turun. 4. *Mau hasil 1 minggu*: Lemak paha itu lemak bandel. Butuh 4-8 minggu buat lihat perubahan nyata. 5. *Tips Tambahan yang Sering Diabaikan* 1. *Pijit paha pakai foam roller 5 menit* setelah olahraga. Lancarin aliran darah, kurangin selulit. 2. *Perhatiin postur*: Punggung bungkuk bikin paha depan tegang dan keliatan besar. 3. *Foto progress tiap 2 minggu*: Kaca sering nipu. Foto lebih jujur. *Timeline realistis*: Kalau defisit kalori 300-500 kkal/hari + olahraga di atas, paha biasanya mulai keliatan beda di minggu ke-4. Full hasilnya 2-3 bulan. #creatorsearchinsights *Yoga untuk tiroid* nggak bisa nyembuhin, tapi bantu banget ngatur hormon, nurunin stres, dan ningkatin energi. Kuncinya: gerakan lembut + fokus ke area leher + napas. Pilih rutenya tergantung jenis tiroid kamu: 1. *Kalau Hipotiroid - Tiroid Lemah, Metabolisme Lambat* Tujuannya: stimulasi kelenjar tiroid, lancar aliran darah ke leher, lawan capek. 1. *Sarvangasana - Kayang Bahu*      Posisi kaki di atas, beban di bahu. Merangsang tiroid langsung. Tahan 30-60 detik.      _Skip_ kalau ada sakit leher atau darah tinggi. 2. *Matsyasana - Pose Ikan*      Lanjutan setelah kayang bahu. Regangkan leher ke belakang. Tahan 30 detik. 3. *Bhujangasana - Pose Kobra*      Angkat dada pelan. Memijat area tiroid dan naikin energi. 3x tahan 20 detik. 4. *Ustrasana - Pose Unta*      Regangan dalam di leher. Lakuin pelan, jangan dipaksa. 5. *Halasana - Pose Bajak*      Tekanan lembut ke tiroid. Tahan 30 detik max. Lakuin 4-5x seminggu. Ini rantai pose yang paling dipake di yoga terapi tiroid. 2. *Kalau Hipertiroid - Tiroid Aktif Berlebihan* Tujuannya: nenangin sistem saraf, nurunin detak jantung, hindari gerakan yang bikin panas. 1. *Savasana - Pose Mayat*      5 menit tiap hari. Ini paling penting buat nurunin stres. 2. *Viparita Karani - Kaki Naik ke Tembok*      Tahan 3-5 menit. Menenangkan jantung yang sering berdebar. 3. *Balasana - Pose Anak*      1-2 menit. Nurunin cemas dan bikin napas pelan. 4. *Forward Bend Lembut*      Paschimottanasana, Uttanasana. Hindari inversi seperti kayang bahu. 3. *Teknik Napas yang Wajib* 1. *Ujjayi Pranayama - Napas Laut*      Napas lewat hidung sambil sedikit menutup tenggorokan, bunyinya “hhaa”. Getaran di leher bantu stimulasi tiroid. 5 menit sehari. 2. *Simhasana - Pose Singa*      Julurkan lidah, buka mulut lebar. Melepas tegang di leher dan rahang. 3. *Neck Roll*      Putar leher pelan 1 menit sebelum mulai. Jangan cepat-cepat. 4. *Aturan Penting Biar Aman* 1. *Jangan paksa pose leher* kalau ada benjolan, gondok, atau nyeri. Konsultasi dokter dulu. 2. *Konsisten > berat*. 15 menit tiap hari lebih ngaruh daripada 1 jam sekali seminggu. 3. *Yoga bantu, tapi obat tetap jalan*. Jangan stop obat tiroid tanpa izin dokter. 4. *Perhatiin sinyal tubuh*. Pusing, mual, jantung berdebar = stop dan istirahat. 5. *Rutinitas 15 Menit Harian untuk Hipotiroid* 1. Neck roll 1 menit 2. Cat-Cow 2 menit 3. Kobra 3x20 detik 4. Bridge Pose 2x30 detik 5. Pose Ikan 1 menit 6. Savasana + Napas Ujjayi 3 menit Lakuin pagi sebelum sarapan biar energi naik sepanjang hari. Biasanya perubahan kerasa di minggu 3-4: tidur lebih nyenyak, capek berkurang, mood lebih stabil. Kamu hipotiroid atau hipertiroid? Aku sesuaikan rutenya biar nggak salah gerakan. #olahragayoga #pejuangsehat

*Hip band resistance panjang* itu resistance band karet panjang yang lingkarannya besar, biasanya 1.5-2 meter. Beda sama hip band mini yang melingkar kecil di paha. Fungsinya buat latihan bokong, paha, pinggul, dan core dengan beban yang bisa disesuaikan. 1. *Kenapa Pakai yang Panjang* 1. *Multifungsi*: Bisa buat upper body, lower body, stretching, dan bantu pull-up. Hip band mini cuma buat kaki & bokong. 2. *Beban progresif*: Panjangnya bikin kamu bisa adjust intensitas. Makin ditarik pendek, makin berat. 3. *Aman buat pemula*: Lebih fleksibel dari dumbbell. Kalau kebesaran beban, tinggal kasih slack. 4. *Harga murah*: 1 set 3-5 level 80-150rb udah cukup buat 6 bulan. 2. *Cara Pilih yang Bagus* Level	Warna Biasa	Beban	Cocok Untuk **Light**	Kuning/Merah	5-10kg	Pemanasan, bahu, pemula **Medium**	Hijau/Biru	10-20kg	Glute bridge, row, squat **Heavy**	Hitam/Ungu	20-35kg	Deadlift, lat pulldown **Extra Heavy**	Abu-abu/Orange	35-50kg	Progresi lanjut *Tips beli*: Pilih bahan latex natural. Yang TPE murah gampang putus dan nggak elastis. Cek review biar nggak bau karet menyengat. 3. *7 Gerakan Andalan Buat Bokong & Paha* Lakuin 3 set, 12-15 repetisi tiap gerakan. Istirahat 30 detik. 1. *Banded Squat*      Injak band, pegang ujung di bahu. Squat seperti biasa. Band nambah beban tanpa bikin punggung sakit. 2. *Glute Bridge with Band Pull*      Tidur telentang, band di paha. Angkat pinggul sambil tarik band ke luar. Rasain bokong kebakar. 3. *Banded Deadlift*      Injak band, tarik ke atas sampai berdiri. Fokus ke paha belakang & bokong. 4. *Standing Lateral Walk*      Injak band, tarik ke atas pegang di pinggang. Jalan menyamping. Oblique & glute medius aktif. 5. *Banded Kickback*      Pegang band di tiang/pegangan pintu. Tendang kaki ke belakang. Bentuk bokong atas. 6. *Seated Row*      Duduk, kaitkan band di kaki. Tarik band ke perut. Punggung atas & lengan ikut kuat. 7. *Assisted Pull-up*      Kaitkan band di pull-up bar, injak ujungnya. Band bantu angkat badan kamu. 4. *Kesalahan yang Bikin Nggak Efektif* 1. *Band terlalu longgar*: Kalau nggak ada resistensi, nggak ada hasil. Pendekin pegangan. 2. *Gerakan cepat & ngasal*: Band itu bikin kamu sadar form. Gerak pelan, 3 detik turun. 3. *Cuma fokus paha*: Bokong butuh mind-muscle connection. Dorong pakai bokong, bukan paha. 4. *Nggak ganti level*: Kalau 15 rep masih gampang, naik level. Otot nggak tumbuh di zona nyaman. 5. *Perawatan Biar Awet 1 Tahun+* 1. *Jangan kena lantai kasar*: Karet gampang tergores. Pakai di atas matras. 2. *Hindari sinar matahari langsung*: Simpan di laci. UV bikin karet getas. 3. *Bersihkan pakai kain lembap*: Jangan pakai alkohol, bikin kering. 4. *Cek retak tiap bulan*: Kalau ada retak kecil, buang. Putus pas latihan bisa nyamber. Hip band panjang itu alat paling “value for money” buat latihan di rumah. Nggak makan tempat, bisa bawa travel, dan progresnya jelas. *“Aku glowing saat berkeringat”* itu bukan efek filter — itu tandanya kulit lembap, aliran darah lancar, dan keringatnya keluar bersih. Kuncinya ada di 3 hal: persiapan sebelum olahraga, perlakuan saat olahraga, dan aftercare setelahnya. 1. *Sebelum Olahraga: Siapin Kulit Biar Nggak Kusam* Keringat itu nggak bikin jerawat, tapi kotoran + keringat + sisa makeup = komedo. 1. *Cuci muka 30 menit sebelum olahraga*      Pakai cleanser ringan. Jangan olahraga dengan makeup atau sunscreen tebal. Nanti pori ketutup dan muncul “sweat rash”. 2. *Sunscreen kalau olahraga pagi di luar*      Pilih yang gel/water-based, label “non-comedogenic”. Keringat + sinar UV = flek hitam. 3. *Hindari skincare berat*      Skip retinol, AHA/BHA, minyak berat 2 jam sebelum olahraga. Kulit sensitif kalau kena gesekan + keringat. 2. *Saat Berkeringat: Biar Glowing, Bukan Bruntusan* 1. *Jangan usap wajah pakai tangan/tisu kasar*      Tepuk pelan pakai handuk bersih yang khusus buat muka. Gesekan bikin iritasi. 2. *Minum air putih*      Dehidrasi = kulit kusam. 500ml sebelum olahraga, teguk kecil tiap 15 menit. 3. *Pilih tempat & pakaian yang adem*      Keringat berlebihan + panas + baju ketat = biang keringat dan iritasi. Bahan katun/DRY-FIT lebih aman. 3. *Setelah Olahraga: 10 Menit Emas* Ini fase paling penting buat “glow”-nya keluar. 1. *Bilas muka dalam 5 menit setelah selesai*      Keringat yang dibiarin kering di kulit bikin pH berantakan dan nyumbat pori. Pakai air dingin/suam, cleanser lembut. 2. *Toner & Hydrating Toner/Essence*      Kulit habis olahraga kehilangan air. Pakai yang ada hyaluronic acid, centella, atau panthenol. 3. *Moisturizer ringan*      Jangan skip pelembap karena “udah berminyak”. Kulit kering malah produksi minyak lebih banyak. 4. *Jangan langsung pakai scrub/masker keras*      Kulit lagi sensitif. Tunggu 2-3 jam kalau mau pakai sheet mask. 4. *Yang Bikin Kulit Malah Kusam Saat Keringatan* 1. *Tidur dengan keringat & keringat kering*      Bikin bakteri numpuk. Mandi wajib kalau mau tidur. 2. *Makan gorengan + gula setelah olahraga*      Inflamasi naik, kulit kusam keesokan harinya. Balik ke protein + buah lebih aman. 3. *Gesekan baju kotor berulang*      Handuk dan baju olahraga dipakai ulang = bakteri. Ganti tiap sesi. 5. *Booster Glowing Alami dari Dalam* Glowing pas keringatan paling kelihatan kalau: - *Tidur 7-8 jam*: Hormon perbaikan kulit kerja malam hari. - *Cukup air 2-2.5L/hari*: Kulit plump = cahaya mantul lebih bagus. - *Makan makanan tinggi antioksidan*: Alpukat, tomat, jeruk, kacang. Lawan radikal bebas dari keringat + polusi. Intinya: keringat itu natural highlight kalau kulitnya bersih dan terhidrasi. Orang yang “glowing saat olahraga” biasanya konsisten cuci muka + minum air + tidur cukup. Still someone who has handled hard things before. This diagnosis does not erase that. And type 2 diabetes is not your identity. 👉 It’s a metabolic condition. 3 Key Form Highlights 1. Are your shoulders fully open? This just means are your arms fully overhead.  If not, you need to work on your overhead mobility. Work on shoulder flexion stretches.  2. Is your pelvis (lower back) open? Don't let your pelvis anteriorly tilt (APT) or open up. Make sure you maintain a closed back aka posterior pelvic tilt.  (PPT)  3. Are you bracing your core? With an open core, this will be difficult to balance especially as a beginner.  Squeeze your core, think rib cage in.  Train the hollow body like a gymnast and this will be much easier.  4. Does a straight body line matter?  Yes and no.  For beginners yes. It's mich easier to learn this skill with proper form. If you learn instead with a banana back, it will be quite difficult to learn other techniques.  If you have experience already, I encourage you to play with the banana back and other variations.  Perfect form is not always needed. However, when learning a skill it is highly encouraged to prevent injury and speed up progression.  As always, shoot me a dm if you need any advice. Full explanation for each move below  Level 30 - Tuck Front Lever Raises  This is a dynamic movement. Dynamic movements utilize your muscles to move throughout a range of motion sometimes even utilizing momentum.  It’s much easier to take yourself through a range of motion compared to just holding it frozen like a statue.  Front lever raises vary in difficulty depending on which shape / progression you use. Don’t bend your arms, or plummet back to the earth.  A good starting point is use the easiest progression, and try for 3-5 sets of 4-6 reps. The key here is quality form, not a bunch of reps aka quantity. If this is too hard, work on hanging knee raises, leg raises, and lat pulldown working to at least 1/2 your bodyweight. Level 35 - Tuck Front Lever  This is an isometric exercise. Moves like this are usually harder then dynamic moves. This is because you literally need to fight gravity pulling you back down to the earth! This move is not mainly core….. it’s mainly back and biceps. The lats are responsible extending your body into the proper position. However, if your back is weak, your core will need to do more work . A flat  back aka parallel to the ground is key here…. along with a slightly retracted or neutral scapula position. If this is too hard, go back to front lever raises or negatives. Work on doing this for 3-6 sets of 5-10s. Do not aim for failure and a bunch of time like 30s here. FORM IS KEY. DM me if you have any questions. BTW, I just started school full time with a bunch of math and science…. so if i don’t get back right away, you know why. BULLISH & BEARISH ENGULFING Pola ini dapat dikenali ketikas terdapat candlestick yang panjangnya melebihu candlestick sebelumnya. Harga low dari bullish candlestick tidak perlu lebih rendah dari bearish candle sebelumnya. namun harga high harus lebih tinggi BULLISH & BEARISH HARAMI Bullish harami ditandai denfan kemunculan candlestick yg lebih kecil daripada candlestick sebelumnya yg merupakan candlestick bearish. sedangkan Bearish harami adalah kebalikannya TWEEZER TOP & BOTTOM TWEEZER BOTTOM merupakan bentuk hammer berdampingan dan ada di dasar penurunan. TWEEZER TOP merupakan inverted hammer/ shooting star yang berdampingan dan berada atas kenaikan PIERCING LINE & DARK CLOUD COVER PIERCING LINE : harga low candlestick bullish HARUS lebih rendah dari candlestick bearish. harga close candlestick bulish HARUS lebih tinggi dari candlestick bearish. PANJANG body candle bullish MINIMAL SETENGAH panjang body candle bearish sebelumnya DARK CLOUD COVER : harga high candle bearish HARUS lebih tinggi dari harga high candlestick bullish sebelumnya. harga close candlestick bearish HARUS lebih rendah dari harga close bullish sebelumnya. Panjang body bearish MINIMAL SETENGAH panjang nodt candle bullish sebelumnya #sahampemula #saham #sahamsyariah #sahamindonesia #sahamprofit

Most people think they need to pick one training style to get stronger. Either daily undulating periodization or block training. But the reality is both have value when you understand how to apply them. DUP is powerful because it exposes your body to different stimuli within the same week. You might have a heavier day, a moderate volume day, and a speed or technique focused day. This allows you to build strength, reinforce skill, and manage fatigue all at once. It keeps training engaging while also giving you more frequent practice with key movements. Block training takes a different approach. Instead of spreading everything out, it focuses your attention on one primary quality at a time. You might spend several weeks building volume and work capacity, then transition into intensification where the loads get heavier and more specific. This creates a clear direction and allows your body to adapt deeply to one goal before shifting focus. The mistake is thinking one is better than the other. DUP is great for maintaining multiple qualities at once. Block training is great for driving a specific adaptation forward with intent. But zoom out for a second. These are just two methods. There are plenty of other ways to get stronger. Linear progression, conjugate systems, autoregulated models, hybrid approaches. They all work when applied correctly. The common denominator is not the system itself, it is your ability to execute it consistently over time. The real question is not which one works. It is which one works for you. Your schedule, your recovery, your stress levels, your experience, your preferences. All of these factors matter. The best program is the one you can actually follow, adjust, and stay consistent with without burning out. Understanding different systems gives you tools. But choosing the right one for your lifestyle is what allows those tools to actually work. That is how you build real strength over time.

Most people don’t struggle with getting stronger because they lack information. They struggle because they have too much of it. Programming gets overcomplicated when you try to account for every possible variable at once. Exercise selection, volume, intensity, frequency, tempo, rest times. All of these matter, but trying to optimize all of them simultaneously is what leads to overanalysis paralysis. You end up thinking instead of training. Strength is built on consistent exposure to the basics. A few key movements, done well, progressed over time. You do not need a perfect program. You need a repeatable one. Something you can execute week after week while making small, measurable improvements. A simple structure works. Pick a main movement. Work within a clear rep range. Leave a couple reps in reserve. Add load or reps over time. That alone will take most beginners and intermediates very far. The irony is that chasing perfection usually leads to inaction. You keep tweaking, adjusting, second guessing. Meanwhile, the person running a simple plan with intent is getting stronger right in front of you. Clarity beats complexity every time. If your program feels confusing, it is probably not effective. Simplify the inputs so you can maximize the output. Focus on execution, consistency, and progression. You do not need more complexity. You need more reps done with intent.

Pain is not the enemy. It is information. If you want to get stronger long term, you need to learn how to interpret what your body is telling you. Not all pain means stop, and not all discomfort means you are making progress. There is a difference between muscular fatigue, connective tissue stress, and true injury signals. Muscular fatigue usually feels like a burn or heaviness. This is often productive and expected when training hard. Tendon or joint discomfort tends to feel more localized, stiff, or sharp, especially under load or at specific ranges. This is where you need to pay attention and adjust. Ignoring these signals is where most people go wrong. They push through everything, stack fatigue, and eventually get forced to stop completely. On the flip side, some people avoid any discomfort at all, which limits adaptation and slows progress. The goal is not to avoid pain. The goal is to understand it. Ask yourself what type of pain you are feeling, when it shows up, and how it changes with load, tempo, and volume. Then make intelligent adjustments. That could mean reducing intensity, controlling tempo, limiting range, or modifying exercise selection. This is how you build resilience. You are not just training muscles, you are training your ability to tolerate and adapt to stress. Strength is not just about how much you can lift. It is about how well you can listen, adjust, and continue progressing without breaking down.

Trying to improve everything at once is one of the fastest ways to stall your strength progress. When you chase too many variables at the same time, your body doesn’t know what to adapt to. Are you trying to get stronger, build endurance, fix technique, increase volume, and add new exercises all at once? That lack of clarity creates noise, and noise kills progress. Strength is a specific adaptation. It requires a clear signal. If your training is too broad, that signal gets diluted. Instead of getting really good at one thing, you stay average at many. This is where most lifters go wrong. They constantly change exercises, tweak form every session, and jump between goals. But without consistency, there is nothing to measure, nothing to refine, and nothing to truly improve. Narrow your focus. Pick a movement. Pick a progression. Give your body a reason to adapt. Mastery comes from depth, not width. If you want to get strong, you need to be intentional. Less noise, more precision.

Most strength athletes don’t fail because of lack of effort. They fail because they don’t manage fatigue. There is a difference between training hard and accumulating fatigue faster than your body can recover from. If every session turns into a max effort grind, your nervous system, joints, and connective tissues fall behind. Performance becomes inconsistent, technique breaks down, and small aches slowly turn into real problems. A big mistake is skipping progression structure. People start too heavy in week one, then have nowhere to go. Instead, you should earn intensity. Open a block at a light to moderate difficulty, around 3 to 4 reps in reserve. This gives you room to build. From there, gradually increase either load, reps, or total work each week. Week two might sit around 3 RIR, week three around 2 RIR, and by week four you are pushing closer to 1 RIR. This creates a clear progression while managing fatigue so you can actually adapt instead of just survive sessions. Another effective approach is using a DUP model, daily undulating periodization. Instead of training the same rep range every session, you rotate stressors. One day might be strength focused with lower reps, another hypertrophy focused with moderate reps, and another more speed or technique focused. This distributes fatigue while still driving progress across multiple qualities. Fatigue is not just muscular. It is systemic. Poor sleep, high stress, inconsistent nutrition, and excessive volume all stack together. You might feel strong in the moment, but you are borrowing from tomorrow’s performance. The fix is to train with intent instead of emotion. Use RIR to guide effort, keep most of your work in that 2 to 4 RIR range early on, and earn the right to push harder as the weeks progress. Focus on stacking quality weeks, not just chasing one big session. If you want to get stronger, you need to manage fatigue first, then express strength. Most people treat the warm up like a formality. Something to just get through before the real work starts. That mindset is exactly why progress stalls and small aches start to show up. Your warm up is where the session actually begins. This is your opportunity to rehearse the exact movement you’re about to load. Not just physically, but neurologically. You are teaching your body how to move before stress is introduced. If you move carelessly here, don’t expect precision when the weight gets heavy. Be intentional with every rep. How are you setting your feet. Are you controlling the eccentric. Are you owning the bottom position. Are you applying the same cues you plan to use under load. This is where you build consistency before intensity. External resistance should not be the first time your body experiences the movement done correctly. Dial in your positions with bodyweight or light loads first. Create tension. Find stability. Feel the muscles you actually want working. This is how you bridge the gap between just moving and actually training. A great session is rarely built on hype alone. It is built on preparation. If you want to get stronger, move better, and stay healthy long term, start treating your warm up like it matters. Because it does.

Most people don’t have a strength problem. They have a preparation problem. Your warm up is not just about getting sweaty or going through random motions. It is about preparing your body for the exact demands of the movement you’re about to perform. If your warm up doesn’t resemble your working sets in some way, you’re leaving performance on the table. Intentional warm ups bridge the gap between rest and execution. They groove your technique, wake up the specific muscles involved, and allow your joints and tendons to gradually tolerate load. This is especially important for movements like dips, pull ups, and squats where positioning and tension dictate everything. Instead of rushing through generic mobility drills, think in layers. Start with general movement to increase temperature. Then transition into specific patterns that mimic your lift. Use feeler sets to dial in bar path, tempo, and control. Each set should have a purpose, not just be a stepping stone to your top set. This is also where you gather data. How does the weight feel today. Are you moving fast or slow. Do you feel stable or shaky. Your warm up tells you exactly how to adjust your session in real time. If you want to get stronger consistently, you cannot treat your warm up like an afterthought. It is the foundation for everything that follows. Train with intention from the very first rep.

Strength isn’t just about effort, it’s about direction. And direction comes from the cues you choose to focus on. When you’re learning an exercise, your brain can only process so much at once. If you try to think about everything, you end up executing nothing with precision. This is where specific cues come in. They simplify complexity into something actionable. A cue is essentially a shortcut for your nervous system. Instead of thinking “engage lats, stabilize core, maintain bar path,” you might think “pull the bar to your ribs” or “stay stacked.” One clear intention produces a cleaner output. The key is understanding that cues are individual. What clicks for one person may not click for another. Some people respond better to internal cues like “squeeze your glutes.” Others perform better with external cues like “push the floor away.” Your job is to find what creates the best movement with the least amount of mental friction. As you get stronger, your cues may evolve. Early on, you need simple and direct. Over time, you refine and layer complexity. But the foundation always stays the same. Clear focus drives consistent execution. If your reps feel inconsistent, it’s usually not a strength issue. It’s a clarity issue. Dial in the right cue, and strength becomes much easier to express. Retired doesn’t mean forgotten. The fights ended.   The lessons didn’t. Everything I learned through Muay Thai, competing, injuries, discipline, recovery, and pushing through hard moments still carries into how I coach, lead, train, and live today. These days, training looks different. Today’s session was: 4-minute VO2 max runs   4-minute recovery walks   4 rounds total Heart rate averaging around 175–180 BPM during the runs, with the goal of getting recovery heart rate back down around 120–130 BPM during the walks. Then after that: hip PT   shoulder PT   mobility work   recovery work   all the fun stuff that comes with years of wear and tear from the fight game. But I still make the time. One of the biggest challenges I face now is not eating like I did during my fight career. Back then we could burn 4,000–6,000 calories a day and recover differently. Now the focus is learning how to adjust my nutrition protocols to align with where my body is now: recovery   longevity   performance   mobility   energy That’s something we’re continuously experimenting with, learning through, and building resources around inside Lifestyle of Fitness. I’m not perfect at it, but that’s part of what I love sharing through coaching and with my team. That’s one of the biggest lessons martial arts taught me: discipline is not about destroying yourself every day. It’s about adapting without losing the standard. Years ago the goal was pushing harder.   Now the goal is: longevity   mobility   recovery   consistency   performance The mindset never left.   The application evolved. That’s something we talked about recently on the podcast with @monstrousitous and we’re diving deeper into again tomorrow with one of my clients who’s lost over 50 pounds and kept it off long term. The real win isn’t going hard for one season. It’s building a system you can evolve with for life. #muaythai #vo2max #mindset #recovery #discipline

🔥 The Spiritual Warm-Up 🔥 Scripture: “In the morning, Lord, you hear my voice; in the morning I lay my requests before you and wait expectantly.” — Psalm 5:3 (NIV) Every workout begins with a warm-up — we stretch, move, and prepare our body for what’s ahead. But how often do we warm up our spirit before facing the day? So many of us rush into our routines — checking messages, grabbing coffee, and diving into the chaos — without ever pausing to prepare our hearts. We want spiritual strength, but we skip the warm-up that awakens our connection with God. David made it a habit: before battles, before decisions, before anything — he prayed. His first movement was spiritual. When we take a few quiet minutes in prayer, worship, or reflection each morning, we tune our hearts to Heaven. Just like our muscles perform better when they’re warm, our soul functions best when it’s aligned with God. The warm-up isn’t wasted time — it’s the foundation for every rep that follows. 💜 Start your day expectant, not anxious. Centered, not scattered. Ready — because your spirit is warmed up. 🙏✨ #FaithFactorFitness #DumbbellsAndDevotion #SpiritualWarmUp #FaithAndFitness #MorningPrayer

🌩 Faith Under Pressure 💪 “Consider it pure joy… whenever you face trials of many kinds, because you know that the testing of your faith produces perseverance.” — James 1:2–4 (NIV) Pressure can feel heavy — the barbell on your chest, the weight of life on your shoulders. But remember: resistance isn’t punishment — it’s preparation. Just like muscle fibers tear to rebuild stronger, God allows “holy tension” to strengthen your spirit. The strain that feels uncomfortable today is building endurance for tomorrow. It’s easy to praise God when life is light — but real growth happens under pressure. Trials are your spiritual workouts, shaping your faith and fortifying your perseverance. So when the weight feels too much, take heart: you’re not lifting alone. God is spotting you. He won’t let the load crush you — He’s using it to strengthen you. 🙏💜 #FaithFactorFitness #DumbbellsAndDevotion #FaithUnderPressure #SpiritualStrength #Perseverance

The Dumbbell Squat to Overhead Press builds strength, coordination, and control when performed with intention. Why is this movement great? Let's dive in on how to best perform or instruct clients on how to perform this exercise: >> Start Position: 📍Stand with feet hip to shoulder width apart 📍Hold dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing in 📍Brace your core >> Squat: 📍Sit hips back and down into a controlled squat 📍Keep chest lifted and knees tracking over toes >> Drive + Press: 📍Push through your feet to stand 📍As you rise, press the dumbbells overhead in one fluid motion >> Return: 📍Lower dumbbells back to shoulders with control 📍Repeat smoothly 🗣️ Key cue: Avoid arching your low back during the press. Keep ribs down and core tight to maintain alignment. Why it matters: ✔ Builds full-body strength and coordination ✔ Reinforces proper squat mechanics under load ✔ Improves overhead stability and control ✔ Encourages mindful sequencing of movement Coaching isn’t just about reps. @coach_mohamad_dxb's journey from childhood obesity to evidence-based coach shows how powerful intentional, mindful movement can be. His approach centers on biomechanics, posterior chain strength, and long-term structural balance. Here’s his Strength Training Progression for Improved Posture: Motor control → stability → load Posterior Chain Strength for Postural Improvement: > Rounded shoulders > Weak mid/lower traps > Weak rhomboids > Poor scapular control ⚡️Exercises: Band Pull-Apart (Regression): Improves scapular retraction strength and neuromuscular control of the posterior shoulder complex. Activates the mid/lower trapezius, rhomboids, and posterior deltoid while minimizing lumbar compensation. Builds a corrective foundation for future loaded rows. > Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. > Hold a band at shoulder height with arms extended. > Maintain neutral spine and engage the core. > Retract the scapulae and pull the band apart until arms align with the torso. > Control the eccentric phase back to start. Kneeling Single-Arm Cable Row (Base Movement): Enhances unilateral scapular stability, anti‑rotational core control, and proper thoracic positioning. Adds load while reinforcing posture. > Kneel in a staggered stance facing the cable machine. > Keep a neutral spine. > Retract the scapula before bending the elbow. > Pull toward the ribcage without trunk rotation. > Return with control while maintaining tension. Dumbbell Bent-Over Row (Bilateral Progression): Strengthens the entire upper posterior chain — latissimus dorsi, erector spinae, and scapular stabilizers. Improves hip hinge mechanics and trunk stability for more advanced pulling patterns. > Stand with feet hip-width apart holding dumbbells. > Hinge at the hips while maintaining neutral spine. > Engage the core and retract the scapulae. > Row weights toward the lower ribcage. > Lower with a controlled eccentric. Stronger in the gym. More capable in real life. We are partnering with NASM CPT @itzythebodyarchitect to show how intentional strength training carries over far beyond the workout floor. When we slow down, focus on control, and move with purpose, we’re not just lifting weights; we’re building confidence for everyday life. These are the kinds of movements that support how you pick things up, carry loads, and move through the world safely and efficiently. 👇 Here’s how it all connects: Deadlift: 🌟 A strength movement where you lift weight from the ground using your legs and hips while keeping your back stable. 🗣️ How? Feet hip-width apart; Grip the bar (or dumbbells) just outside your legs; Keep chest up, back flat; Push through your heels; Stand tall, squeezing glutes at the top; Lower with control >> Real Life Translation: Carrying Heavy Things Picking up heavy boxes, loading your trunk, moving furniture, grabbing your kid off the ground ✅ Deadlift Benefits: > Improves lower back durability > Builds total-body strength > Improves posture when lifting in daily life > Reinforces proper lifting mechanics (when done correctly!) Farmer's Carries: 🌟 Walking while holding heavy weights in each hand, forcing your body to stabilize. 🗣️ How? Hold dumbbells or kettlebells at your sides; Stand tall (don’t lean!); Keep core tight; Walk slow and controlled; If doing stairs: step steady, stay balanced >> Real Life Translation: Carrying groceries upstairs; carrying luggage, laundry baskets, etc.—especially on stairs ✅ Farmer's Carries Benefits: > Builds grip strength > Strengthens core and posture > Improves balance and coordination > Trains your body to handle uneven, real-world loads The gym isn’t separate from your life, it prepares you for it. Dynamic: Lateral Tube Walking > Place a band/tube just above the knees, mid-calf (lower-leg), or at the ankles Pro-tip: The lower the band, the harder the exercise. > Stay in an athletic stance with slight knee bend and hips back > Step side to side with control ✔ Key cue: Keep toes forward and maintain constant band tension 🏀 Dynamic: Squat to Overhead Reach > Lower into a controlled squat with chest lifted > As you stand, reach arms overhead in one smooth motion ✔ Key cue: Avoid arching the low back.
