These exercises will work 3 of your 4 rotator cuff muscles. Need more shoulder help? Comment “Shoulder” and we will send you a complimentary 5-day shoulder series to help you overcome your shoulder pain and improve mobility.  The first exercise emphasizes external rotation of the shoulder and will target the Infraspinatus and Teres Minor muscles. The teres minor is not painted, but lies directly inferior to the infraspinatus. The second exercise emphasizes internal rotation of the shoulder and will work the subscapularis muscle (also not painted). The subscapularis is located deep in your armpit. It covers the entire concave side of the shoulder blade (it’s between your ribs and shoulder blade).  Your rotator cuff muscles don’t just move the arm as shown in the video, one of their major functions is to keep the shoulder inside the shoulder socket. With that in mind, a variety of farmer carries will also work all 4 of the rotator cuff muscles if moving the shoulder is too painful to do right now. The cushion is necessary to prevent you from compensating. By squeezing it the entire time, it forces you to isolate the movement to your shoulder joint so that you don’t involve your shoulder blade.  Have any questions? Drop them in the comments.

🚨 Still dealing with neck pain or tightness? 🚨 Comment “Neck” below and I’ll give you our gentle, detailed neck series- no cost. This stretch hits the levator scapulae, upper traps, paraspinals, and suboccipitals… all the muscles that love to stay tight and cranky. Move gently. Cranking your head down will only make your body guard harder. Think of this as a reset button that gives you relief without the fight. Here’s the truth: stretching alone rarely fixes neck pain for good. It might help for a few minutes or a day, but the tightness almost always returns. What actually works long term is building strength and control. If you have been stretching your neck for weeks with no lasting relief, it is a sign your muscles need strength, not more stretching. “But won’t strengthening make me tighter?” Nope. That tight feeling is your body protecting a weak joint. When you build strength, the nervous system finally relaxes and lets go. Drop your questions below and don’t forget to comment “Neck” so I can send you the full series.

Upper back feeling stiff or locked up? 👀 We don’t yet have a free series for upper back relief… but if you’d want one, drop a “yes!” in the comments so we know! ⬇️ Stress + too much sitting = shallow breaths, tight ribs, and tension that builds up fast. When your ribs stop moving, your upper back can start screaming. Here’s the good news 👉 the muscles between your ribs can be trained just like any other muscle. Breathwork is one of the most overlooked (and most powerful) ways to open things up. While in the position in the video, try these drills: 💨 Deep breath in → squeeze your abs → hold → relax the abs then slowly exhale every last bit of air. 💨 Quick inhale → then forcefully exhale until you think there’s nothing left (and then keep going). 💨 Slow, controlled breaths in and out — calm and steady. 💨 Big inhale → then sneak in another inhale when you think you can’t → exhale fully. Experiment with nose vs. mouth breathing to feel the difference in your ribs. This kind of training unlocks your ribcage so you can move, breathe, and feel better in everything else you do. ➡️ Want us to create a full free upper back series? Comment “Yes!” and let us know! #backpain #backpainrelief #upperbackpain #backstretch #mobilitytraining

Here’s our top 3 glute exercises to help you build that cake. Have hip pain and need something easier than these moves? Comment “Hip” and we will send you our no cost hip relief series. There are obviously many other excellent glute exercises out there.  We wanted to highlight one exercise that lengthens the glute fibers to maximal shreddage and another exercise that burns the glutes in a shortened position. We want to strengthen the muscles in both their lengthened and shortened state. The second exercise is arguably the most deceivingly difficult glute exercise you will ever do. Again, it is a hip hinge, but the emphasis is on the glute in a mid-range of motion. By keeping your weight forward over your toe (without the heel lifting) you will find the glute starts to shake and freak out very quickly. Moving slowly in a small range of motion will quickly get you to the point of fatigue and wanting to fall over. All of these exercises can be loaded (and doing so can actually make it easier to feel the glute fire up), but make sure to practice without weight first if you haven’t tried these. IT Band Pain? Try this ball trick at home!  Do you need more than a massage to help you? Comment “Hip” and we will send you a free hip mobility and strengthening series to help you overcome pain. The TFL muscle (Tensor Fasciae Latae) on the side of the hip turns into the IT band which connects to the outside of the knee. Some of your glute max fibers also turn into the IT band.  In some instances, people experience a sciatica-like sensation down the side of the leg to the knee that can be described as throbbing, aching, or electric. Some peeps call this “pseudosciatica.” The TFL, glute medius, and piriformis are some muscles that can create this “referred” pain into other areas of the hip or leg.  Massaging the TFL can help to alleviate these pains. If the pain does dissipate with a massage, then that is a sign that you may want to also strengthen this muscle! The TFL is a hip abductor, assists the internal rotator of the hip, and assists in hip flexion. So, any of those motions will strengthen it. The free hip series above will provide you with ideas on how to hit all 3 of those motions.  The ball in the video is from @Tune Up Fitness Please do not do this massage against glass like the video. Do it against the wall or, for more intensity, on the floor.

Here’s how to choose a better pushup variation for strength and size…  1 Choose a variation that limits you to 6–12 reps. Feet elevated, deficit pushups, weighted vest, tempo reps. If you can do more than 15 reps straight, it’s too easy.  Build up to 12 reps before advancing… 1. Regular pushups 2. Feet elevated pushups 3. Side to side pushups 4. Feet elevated side to side pushups 5. Assisted one arm pushups 6. Feet elevated assisted one arm pushups 7. One Arm pushups (Use Cluster Sets if needed) 8. Feet elevated one arm pushups 2 Control the tempo. Lower for 3–4 seconds. Pause at the bottom. Explode up. That’s how you increase mechanical tension.. the single most important variable for hypertrophy. 3 Train close to failure. By rep 8–12, you should be near failure — where your form starts to break down and one more rep would get ugly. If you’re stopping while it still feels easy, you’re leaving gains on the table. 4 Track your sets, reps, and variations. Just like you’d log your bench numbers, log your pushup progress. Add reps, make the variation harder (the same as adding weight). That’s progressive overload with bodyweight.  Bottom line.. Pushups only build muscle when you make them hard enough to matter. When you’re doing 20-30 reps a set the first 20-25 reps are too easy.  For my pushup progression video guide, comment “PUSHUP” and I’ll send it over for FREE. Balance training is not just about preventing falls or improving coordination. It is also powerful brain training. When you challenge your balance, you activate multiple regions of the brain simultaneously including the cerebellum (movement precision and motor learning), the vestibular system (spatial orientation and equilibrium), the prefrontal cortex (focus, attention, decision making), and the hippocampus (memory and spatial awareness). This is one reason balance work has been associated with improvements in cognition, reaction time, body awareness, and even long term brain health. Now add controlled breathing to the equation. When you focus on a slow controlled exhale during balance exercises, you create deeper core activation that helps stabilize the spine and pelvis, improving balance from the inside out. At the same time, slower breathing helps calm the nervous system, reducing excess tension and improving your ability to stay focused and steady under challenge. Core activation + nervous system regulation = double whammy. This is why breathing and balance together can become such a powerful neurological practice. One of the most interesting effects of intermittent hypoxic training may be what happens in the brain. You can do it at actual altitude or by controlling your breathing. During controlled exposure to moderate altitude, the body responds to lower oxygen availability by increasing circulation and blood flow, including to the brain. Researchers have explored how this temporary physiological stress may help “prime” the nervous system by increasing cerebral blood flow, activating adaptive pathways, and challenging the brain to become more efficient under stress. Many participants notice: • increased mental clarity • sharper focus • elevated alertness • calmer breathing • improved mind-body connection At HYPOXiX, we combine intermittent hypoxic exposure with controlled breathing, movement, mobility, and cognition-based exercise to create a unique brain-body training experience. The goal is not simply harder training. It is learning how to breathe, focus, regulate, and move more efficiently under challenge. Taking 5 minutes at the top of your lunch break to combine core activation with full body movement can completely shift your energy for the second half of the day. Using the Ab-Ribbon together with controlled breathing during a compound movement like a squat helps reconnect the deep core system while training a highly functional movement pattern. As you slow the breath and emphasize the exhale, the diaphragm, abdominal wall, pelvic floor, and rib mechanics begin working together more efficiently. This can help reduce unnecessary tension, improve posture and stability, and calm the nervous system at the same time. Unlike traditional “core workouts” that isolate the abs, these short HYPOXiX-style movement snacks integrate breathing, strength, balance, and mobility simultaneously. In just a few minutes, you can increase circulation, wake up the hips and spine, improve body awareness, and reset from long periods of sitting or stress. A simple place to start: • Inhale through the nose as you lower into the squat • Long controlled exhale as you stand • Feel the Ab-Ribbon gently connect the lower ribs and abdominal wall during the exhale • Move slowly and smoothly for 5 minutes Small consistent movement breaks like this throughout the week can improve how you breathe, move, focus, and recover — without needing a full workout. One of the most overlooked reasons people experience persistent lower back tension is that they never fully connect to their breathing core while standing. When the deep core system isn’t actively supporting you against gravity, the body often defaults into an overextended posture where the ribs flare, the pelvis tips forward, and the lower back muscles stay constantly “on” just to hold you upright. Your back becomes the stabilizer instead of the diaphragm, deep abdominals, pelvic floor, and obliques working together as a pressure system. This is where breathing matters. A full exhale helps bring the ribs down, engage the deep abdominal wall, and create better alignment between the rib cage and pelvis. The result is less compressive stress on the lumbar spine and less reliance on the lower back muscles to keep you standing. In many cases, lower back discomfort is not simply a “weak back.” It’s a body that has lost access to efficient pressure management and core support during everyday posture and movement. When you learn how to organize your body around the breath: • the pelvis can stack more naturally • the ribs stop drifting upward • the obliques begin assisting with stability • and the lower back finally gets a chance to relax This is why breathing mechanics can completely change the way standing, walking, lifting, and even exercise feel. Many people think their mobility is limited by “tight muscles.” But often it’s limited by incomplete exhalation. If you never fully empty the lungs, the rib cage stays elevated, the spine stays more compressed, and the nervous system remains slightly guarded. That makes it much harder to access true hip extension, rotation, and deep core control. This half kneeling position is powerful because it combines: • hip mobility • pelvic positioning • rib cage control • deep abdominal activation • breath driven nervous system downregulation As you reach a longer, more complete exhale, you may notice: • less tension in the hip flexors • better glute connection • improved spinal movement • deeper core engagement • more space in the body without forcing the stretch The goal is not to “stretch harder.” The goal is to create enough internal support and relaxation that the body finally allows more movement. Use the exhale to create mobility from the inside out. Join my 9 week collective to learn how to do this…all the time! #Breathwork #MobilityTraining #CoreTraining #HipMobility

A deep exhalation can dramatically improve your ability to target the glutes during movements like a hip bridge because it changes the position of the pelvis, activates the deep core, and reduces unnecessary compensation from the lower back. Here’s what’s happening mechanically: When most people do a bridge, they instinctively arch the lumbar spine to “lift higher.” The problem is: • the spinal erectors take over • the ribs flare • the pelvis tips forward (anterior tilt) • the glutes lose mechanical leverage So instead of true hip extension from the glutes, the movement becomes lumbar extension from the low back. A long, forced exhale helps reverse this pattern. During a full exhale: • the ribs come down • the deep abdominal wall activates • intra-abdominal pressure reorganizes • the pelvis gently posteriorly tilts • the diaphragm ascends • the nervous system shifts toward more controlled stabilization This creates a more stable trunk so the glutes can become the primary driver of hip extension. In other words: The exhale “locks” the spine into a better position so the glutes can move the femur without the lower back trying to create motion. In a hip bridge specifically: As you exhale deeply before lifting, think: 1. Pull ribs downward 2. Slightly tuck pelvis 3. Maintain abdominal pressure 4. Push through heels 5. Lift from the glutes, not the spine You’ll often immediately feel: • less low-back tension • more hamstring and glute recruitment • better pelvic control • stronger deep-core activation This is also why combining a forced exhale with tactile feedback like the Ab-Ribbon can be powerful. The exhale helps organize the pressure system internally, while the Ab-Ribbon gives external sensory feedback so you can actually feel the abdominal wall narrowing and stabilizing during the bridge. The result is often: • improved glute isolation • reduced lumbar compensation • better core-to-hip integration • more efficient force transfer through the pelvis Over time, this can help retrain movement patterns so the glutes become more dominant during walking, squatting, lunging, climbing stairs, and athletic movement instead of constantly overusing the lower back. Most people try to strengthen their core by adding more tension. But sometimes the missing piece is actually the exhale. A forced exhale helps activate the deep abdominal system, especially the obliques and transverse abdominis, by increasing internal pressure and creating a stronger connection between the rib cage and pelvis. When paired with Ab-Ribbon, you get immediate feedback into where the breath is moving and whether the obliques are truly engaging. As the ribs narrow and the exhale lengthens: • the obliques begin to wrap and stabilize • the deep core reflexively activates • the neck and shoulders often stop overworking • the nervous system begins to downshift This is why controlled breathing can feel both strengthening and calming at the same time. You are not just training muscles. You are training pressure, coordination, and regulation. 6 breaths per minute. 6 breaths to strength. Most people only learn how to “brace.” But your core also needs to learn how to release. An engaged inhale teaches the diaphragm, deep core, and rib cage to expand with tension and stability. This can improve spinal support, posture, and force production during movement. A released inhale teaches the body to let go of unnecessary gripping. This is critical for reducing chronic tension patterns that often contribute to lower back pain, shallow breathing, neck tension, and poor pelvic alignment. The problem: Most people are stuck in one strategy all day. Either: • over-bracing • sucking in • rib flare • gripping the low back • or collapsing completely True core function is the ability to transition between engagement and release. That’s where the Ab-Ribbon becomes powerful. The Ab-Ribbon gives tactile feedback so you can actually FEEL: • 360° expansion • deep abdominal activation • rib cage positioning • and how breath changes your core connection Inside the HYPOXiX method, we train both engaged and released breathing patterns during movement so your nervous system learns when to stabilize and when to let go. Ein Muskulöser Körper braucht ein starkes Fundament und das bekommst du durch Kniebeuge Varianten.  ➡️ Level 1: Kniebeuge ➡️ Level 2: Ausfallschritte  ➡️ Level 3: Bulgarien Split Squat ➡️ Level 4: Kosaken Kniebeuge  ➡️ Level 5: Pistol Squat  Trainiere deine Beine 2x die Woche. Kombiniere die Level in deinem Training zb. Zuerst Ausfallschritte und als zweite Übung Kniebeugen.  Auf welchem Level bist du?  #legday

Die größten Fitness Fallen bei Männern 30+ ⬇️ ➡️ Du bist übermotiviert und entscheidest dich dazu jeden Tag 100 Liegestütze zu machen. Zu anfangs hat man kleinere Erfolge weil es besser ist als garnichts zutun und wenn kein weiterer Fortschritt kommt (weil das Progressive stärker werden fehlt) dann verliert man die Motivation. ✅️ Mache richtiges Krafttraining. Werde Progressiv in den Grundübungen stärker (Klimmzüge, Dips, Kniebeugen,...). ➡️ Meist werden mehr als 2x HIIT Workouts die Woche gemacht. Weil HIIT Training macht Spaß, man kann sich ordentlich auspowern, man schwitzt....aber es ist für den Körper enorm anstrengend. Du brennst aus. ✅️ Mache maximal 2x die Woche ein HIIT Training. Der Fokus sollte beim "klassischem Krafttraining" sein. ➡️ Oft werden Mahlzeiten ausgelassen. Jetzt ist keine Zeit dafür. Ich kann ja Später noch essen. Die Folge ist das der Körper nicht die Nährstoffe bekommt die er braucht um sich weiterzuentwickeln. Um Muskeln und Kraft aufzubauen.  ✅️ Koche vor oder Nutze Shakes um dir Zeit zu sparen. Plane deine "Pausen" und nimm dir die Zeit zum essen. Es ist dein Körper und Zeit hat man nicht, die nimmt man sich.  ➡️ Die Folge von schlechter Planung und auch von Mahlzeiten ausfallen lassen, ist das man seine Proteine nach Gefühl ist. Meist reicht es nicht aus und die Muskulatur hat keinen Baustoff um sich weiterzuentwickeln und sich ordentlich zu regenerieren. ✅️ Koche vor damit du ordentlich versorgt bist und beschäftige dich für eine Woche mal mit den Nährstoffen der Lebensmittel die du isst. Du bekommst dann ein gutes Wissen darüber was für Mengen benötigt werden um auf seinen Proteinbedarf zu kommen.  Wenn du Fragen dazu hast dann schreibe mir gerne einen Kommentar. #muscle
Die richtige Entscheidung 🤣👍 #muscle
Meine Lieblings Übung für den Bizeps ist der Ring Curl. 👍 Was ist deine Bizeps Lieblings Übung? #muscle

Nicht Muskel für Muskel. Sondern Bewegungsmuster. So geht Ganzkörper Training 👍💪🏻 Mache insgesamt 6 Übungen, eine aus jeder Kategorie: ➡️ Drücken: Liegestütz, Dips, Pike Push Ups, ➡️ Kniebeuge: Kniebeuge, Ausfallschritte, Bulgarien Split Squats, ➡️ Ziehen: Pull Up, Rudern, ➡️ Hüftbeuge: Kreuzheben, Hip Thrust, Beckenheben, ➡️ Core/Rotation: Plank, Side Plank, Hollow Body Hold, ➡️ Plyo + Power: Sprünge, Sprinten, Muscle Up, Wenn du Fragen dazu hast dann schreibe mir einen Kommentar. #muscle

Hör auf jeden Tag 50+ Liegestütze zu machen. Damit bekommst du keinen Athletischen Körper. Zu Anfangs bekommst du ein paar Erfolge und es ist auch eine nette Challenge.  Mache es lieber so: ✅️ 3 bis 4 Krafttrainings die Woche (Ganzkörper oder Oberkörper/Unterkörper Training) ✅️ Nutze intensivere Liegestütz Varianten oder Dips ✅️ Trainiere in einem Wiederholungsberreich unter 15. ✅️ Wer viel drückt muss auch ziehen (Klimmzüge, Rudern,...) ✅️ Besorge dir einen Trainingsplan  Wenn du Fragen dazu hast dann schreibe mir gerne einen Kommentar. #strength

Wenn du T Ziehen machst, dann bekommst du ⬇️ ✅️ Kraft+Muskelaufbau im oberen Rücken ✅️ bessere Körperhaltung  ✅️ gesündere Schulter  Mache diese Übung am Ende deines Trainings. Nach den Grundübungen wie Klimmzüge, Dips,... #muscle

Verändere etwas oder du wirst weiterhin keine Resultate haben. Ich möchte dir direkt und ehrlich das hier sagen, damit du deine Ziele erreichst und ich weiß das dir genau diese 3 Dinge Probleme bereiten. Du willst einen starken Athletischen Körper. Du und ich wissen das es dir wichtig ist. Aber du kommst keinen Schritt weiter. Das sind die 3 Dinge die du verändern musst: ➡️ SCROLLING - du hast möglicherweise genau jetzt in der letzten Stunde durch Instagram oder TikTok gescrollt. Ich weiß "du hast keine Zeit" für ein 60 Minuten Training oder 15 Minuten um dir eine Proteinreiche Mahlzeit zu machen.  ➡️ THINKING - du denkst darüber nach wie und was du am besten machen solltest. Doch das Nachdenken hindert dich daran wirklich etwas zu tun. Zu beginnen. ➡️ WAITING - die Gesundheit wartet auf niemanden. Du kannst zu jederzeit Progress machen, an jedem Ort und unter egal welchen Umständen. Aber du sabotierst dich selbst indem du wartest. 🗣 Als Coach, tut es mir nicht leid das ich dir das so direkt gesagt habe. Manchmal brauchen wir direkte ehrliche Worte. Wenn du einen Athletischen Körper hast, der Stark ist, dann wirst du froh darüber sein das ich dir das heute gesagt habe. Du schaffst das!! Hole dir das was du willst!! Let's go!! #athleticbody #fitness

Du machst immer 15 Wiederholungen oder sogar noch mehr? Und so richtige Erfolge hast du nicht? 🤔 Ich habe viele Jahre meiner Trainingszeit verschwendet weil ich in einem ähnlichen Wiederholungsberreich trainiert habe.....leider mit wenig Erfolg. Erst seit dem ich mich darauf fokussiere stärker zu werden und zunehmend mehr Muskulatur aufzubauen, habe ich auch sichtbare Erfolge.  Muskeln wachsen nur wenn sie "neuen" Reizen ausgesetzt sind denen sie sich anpassen müssen.  Wenn du noch nicht bewusst progressiv trainierst und den Fokus darauf legst stärker zu werden, dann empfehle ich dir folgendes: ✅️ Nimm die nächst schwerere Übung (zb. knieende Liegestütze ➡️ Liegestütze) oder erhöhe das Gewicht (zb. Dips mit eigenem Körpergewicht ➡️ Dips mit Zusatzgewicht) bis du nur noch 5 Wiederholungen schaffst. ✅️ Bleibe bei dieser Übung oder dem Gewicht bis du 6 - 7 Wiederholungen schaffst. ✅️ Erhöhe das Gewicht wieder bzw. Nimm die nächst schwerere Übung und fang das ganze von vorne an. Das ist progressives Krafttraining und wird dir dabei helfen Muskeln aufzubauen und einen Athletischen Körper zu bekommen. #muscle

Explosiveness Exercises for Tennis💥🎾 Part 2: Rotational Power & Transfer Tennis is rotation. If you can’t create, transfer, and express rotational force fast, power stays unused. This is how we train rotational explosiveness for heavier groundstrokes, faster serves, and better shot quality 👇 🔹 1. Med Ball Rotational Throw → Pure rotational power from the ground up. 🔹 2. Med Ball Shot Put Throw → Horizontal force production with aggressive intent. 🔹 3. Half-Kneeling Open Stance Throw → Isolate hip-to-core transfer while controlling the base. 🔹 4. Open Stance Throw → Match-specific power expression in realistic tennis positions. 🔹 5. Reactive Med Ball Rotational Throw → Train timing, reactivity, and elastic power under speed. 🔹 6. Battle Rope Rotational Shadow Swings → High-speed rotational endurance + rhythm. 🔹 7. Rotational Sled Pull → Build force through rotation and project it forward. ✅ Rotation starts from the ground ✅ Power must move through the core ✅ Speed + timing decide the outcome 📌 Strength creates power. Rotation delivers it. More drills, structure & programming → link in bio #tennisperformance #tennisworkout #tennisfitness #rotationalexercises

Upper Body Explosiveness for Tennis🎾 Part 1: Powerful strokes don’t come from strength alone. They come from how fast you can express force. Tennis Surface Comparison 🧱🌱 Why Surfaces Shape Your Game & Training Every tennis court surface tells its own story – not just in how the ball bounces, but in how your body moves, how long you need to sustain intensity, and even where the risk of injury lies. 📊 (📌 Source: Rajkumar, 2025 – The Effect of Different Court Surfaces on Tennis Player Performance and Injury Risk) Let’s break it down ⬇️ 🌱 Grass Court • Rally Duration (ø): 5.4 sec • Unforced Errors (ø per match): 21.1 • Serve Speed (ø): 192.3 km/h • Injury Rate: 6.2% (mainly muscle strains due to explosive sprints) • Fatigue Score: 5.3 / 10 🏟️ Hard Court • Rally Duration (ø): 7.8 sec • Unforced Errors (ø per match): 25.6 • Serve Speed (ø): 185.2 km/h • Injury Rate: 9.7% (highest risk, mostly knees/ankles) • Fatigue Score: 6.1 / 10 🧱 Clay Court • Rally Duration (ø): 15.6 sec • Unforced Errors (ø per match): 32.3 • Serve Speed (ø): 170.4 km/h • Injury Rate: 3.5% (lowest risk, but high muscular fatigue) • Fatigue Score: 7.5 / 10 ⚡ Why this matters for athletes: If you know your surface-specific demands, you can tailor your off-court training. ✅ On grass, prioritize explosiveness & reaction. ✅ On hard court, focus on strength, deceleration & joint health. ✅ On clay, build endurance & technical stability. That’s how you train smarter, not just harder – and keep your body ready for every season of the tour. If you want more information check the link in bio 👀 #tennistraining #tennisfitness #tennisworkout #australianopen #tennisconditioning

🎾 The 6 Explosiveness Essentials Every Tennis Player Needs 💥 If you want to move faster, jump higher, and react sharper on court. You don’t just need to train explosiveness. You need to train it smart. With structure, intent, and tennis-specific purpose.👇 🔹 1. Potentiation → Wake up your nervous system with quick reactive drills. E.g. A-Skips, Pogo Jumps, Hip Switches. 🔹 2. Vertical Explosiveness → Build lift-off for overheads, smashes, and vertical reach. E.g. Countermovement Jumps, Squat Jumps. 🔹 3. Horizontal Power → Accelerate and cover ground with max intent. E.g. Triple Broad Jumps, Standing Long Jump. 🔹 4. Lateral Explosiveness → Power your side-to-side movement for defense and court coverage. E.g. Half-Kneeling Lateral Bounds, Skater Jumps. 🔹 5. Quick Ground Contact → Be reactive off the bounce — short contact, fast output. E.g. Single-Leg Drop Jumps, Reactive Pogos. 🔹 6. Landing Control → You can’t explode without being able to absorb. E.g. Single-Leg Landings, Stick-and-Hold Variations. ✅ Build your explosiveness layer by layer. Each element feeds the next — from power output to injury resilience. 📌 Want me to build your program? How to Structure Your Performance Session 🎾💥 If you want to move faster, hit harder, and last longer on court. It’s not just what you train, but how you sequence it. Fast, reactive drills switch your body into “go-mode” for explosive output. 3️⃣ Sprint Work Sprint work always comes early because speed demands a fresh system. Power, reactivity, and posture degrade with fatigue. 4️⃣ Explosiveness – Lower & Upper Body Next: convert strength into speed. Low-rep jumps and throws develop the fast-twitch power tennis needs, especially under pressure. 5️⃣ Strength – Lower Body Heavy lifts now build force capacity. Isometric holds protect tendons, boost joint integrity and prepare your body for deceleration on court. 8️⃣ Cooldown & Recovery Bring the system back down. Recovery starts before you leave the gym. Downregulation sets you up for better adaptation. ✅ Each phase builds on the last. Next-level ONE ARM STRENGTH 💪🏼😎 MUSCULAR BALANCE is an important factor both in training and everyday life and, although anatomically no one is perfectly even, it’s good to be aware of your deviations and keep your body functioning as well as possible. ☺️ This session acted more of a rehab session for me as my problematic left pec was so incredibly tight that the only way to stretch it out safely was to hang and load the muscles with my bodyweight. To skip ahead of the story - I succeeded in releasing the pec but I might have DOMS tomorrow. 🤭 ⚠️ HOW MANY? - The honest answer is however many you can! ♥️ I understand that this is one of the harder workouts that I have shared and it might not be accessible to everyone.  ✅ ADAPT - If one arm is too much, stick to double handed holds and perform the rotating stretch with your feet on the floor. However, if you would eventually like to progress towards one arm work, throw a towel (easier) or resistance band (medium difficulty) over the bar and hold on to that with one hand. This way you can slowly get used to the transfer of weight and the shift in your centre of gravity.  MY WORKOUT: 1️⃣ O/A LEG RAISE - 5-7 reps per side 2️⃣ O/A ROTATIONS - 3-5 rotations per side 3️⃣ O/A DEADLIFTS - 5-7 reps per arm (3-5 if heavier) 4️⃣ O/A HANGS - however long I can manage, 25-30 sec holds today 5️⃣ TTB - usually 7-10 reps, today 5-6 reps per set 6️⃣ OBLIQUE CRUNCHES - usually 10 reps, today 5 per set I hope you can find some elements to add into your workouts to help you strengthen your shoulders & grip! ☺️ #calisthenicstraining #calisthenicsworkout #onearmhang  #calistenia #onearmstrength

Boosting my BOX JUMP: Re-introducing PLYOMETRICS 💪🏼😎 As a personal trainer, it is important to occasionally also showcase my personal and professional strengths so that the right people can find me. Nowadays my page has a lot of calisthenics content but I was a strength & conditioning coach first plus I work with sports rehab clients and the elderly. There are many strings to my bow. 😌 ⚠️ This is a personal session so I am not encouraging copying this session exercise for exercise, but you absolutely can introduce the individual elements at reasonable intensities to reap the benefits. ☺️  ✅ Plyometric training can be a lot of fun, but it isn’t something that most people incorporate into their sessions. That’s okay, you don’t have to do crazy elements, however I would like you to know that maintaining at least some type of explosive or plyometric movement in your training programmes is going to help keep your ligaments and joints strong.  I will share more on plyometric training in the future and will make a whole post on preparing for/performing box jumps for those who would like to add the exercise to their training OR those who want to find out what their max height is! 👀 💪🏼 My current box jump is 42”(106cm) at 5’9,5”(176cm). Surprisingly, I had not lost any height on my jumps despite not doing this for years. Just goes to show how a thorough training programme over the years - that covers a multitude of elements - will build you a resilient body! This is the main reason why I always encourage variety (and not overly restrictive training plans) as you make improvements across the board over time and don’t risk overtraining or injuring yourself.  If you have any specific requests on training advice or tips, let me know! ☺️ #boxjumps #longjump #standinglongjump #reverselunge #reversenordiccurls

CORE strength final boss? Pseudo Plank/ROLL-OUTS💪🏼😮‍💨 The best part about most calisthenics skills is that they are scalable all the way from beginner stages to elite and this exercise is no different! FIRST STAGE, accessible today: ✅ KNEELING ROLL-OUTS - align your knees, hips & shoulders and start with your body at a 45 degree angle in relation to the floor. Tuck pelvis under, keep ribs tucked (“ribs to hips”) and start pushing the bar down and forward.  ☝🏼 Go as far as you can without compromising your technique. Don’t worry, your range will improve shortly over the upcoming weeks! SECOND STAGE, accessible in a few weeks’/months’ time: ✅ FULL ROLL-OUT NEGATIVES - start on your feet, keeping core hollow. Keep shoulders over bar/wrists until you have pushed yourself far enough forward to start to feel the trembling in your core. Drop onto your knees, keeping the core controlled and push the bar further out. Upon returning, keep hips tucked and avoid arching (otherwise so easy to let happen).  ☝🏼 If the barbell method is too unsteady, switch to sliders and bring arms back in one at a time. I will link a slider workout to this video for easy access.  ✅ SLOW REPS - once confident, start slowing repetitions down. Keep knees off the ground for as long as you can and extend arms so far overhead that your body ends up horizontal.  ☝🏼 Slow kneeling negatives allow to fix technique whenever needed, so return to easier variations as often as you feel like. THIRD STAGE, accessible in some months’ time: ✅ SINGLE LEG ROLL-OUTS - for when you are getting used to (or bored of?) regular repetitions, start doing single leg reps. You will boost your straight leg and hip strength in addition to loading your core with more resistance (due to less help through the legs).  ☝🏼 Fully kneeling option might be available to you much sooner so worth giving it a go! FINAL RESULT: ✅ PSEUDO PLANK - walk your hands forward or your feet back from your regular plank. With regular roll-out practice, your strength and range will improve drastically! 😍 Enjoy! 💪🏼😎 #calisthenicsuk #calisthenicstraining #calisthenicsworkout #coreworkout #calistenia

UNORTHODOX approach for solid FRONT LEVERS 💪🏼😏 If you’re struggling to keep your hips ELEVATED or EXTENDED during front lever holds, these drills might be perfect for you!  Main POSTURE TIPS before you start: ✳️Ribs tucked, pelvis tucked - you want a tabletop torso.  ✳️Heels or toes on the box as long as you don’t push through your legs. Your feet are for support only.  ✳️Shoulderblades retracted (pulled back) for optimal isometric strength in your upper back. EXERCISES: 1️⃣ SUSPENDED HIP EXTENSION - this teaches your body to work through your lower abdomen instead of your lower back and ensures you are engaging your pelvic floor muscles, resulting in a strong straight line through the hips. Avoid pushing through your legs or pulling through arms; this is all about the hips and deep core. 5-10 rep sets to reasonable fatigue.  2️⃣ WEIGHTED ASSISTED F/L - this drill improves your scapular strength for holding your body up in the full lever. Don’t arch your back, don’t power push your legs, simply maintain full body tension (esp core & glutes). Align all joints and hold for as long as possible, just as if you were hanging from the bar or rings. 10 second holds, work your way up to your b/w on the bar.  3️⃣ WEIGHTED INV. ROW - whether you wish to improve your upper back strength, posture or dream of doing FRONT LEVER PULLS one day, this is the exercise to choose. Ensure your shoulders are away from your ears and scapula retracted. Try different weights to see where your max lies. 3-5 reps for strength, 5-7 reps for technique work.  4️⃣ INVERTED ROW - Same exercise, no extra resistance. It is still more challenging than regular inverted rows from the floor and, if you are looking for an additional step between this and the previous exercise, set yourself up on a decline to have your legs higher than your torso. 8-12 reps.  5️⃣ FALSE GRIP INV. ROW - for a boost to your forearm strength or to bulletproof your wrists for muscle-ups, now is a good time to work in your F/G sets - two birds, one stone. 3-5/5-7 reps per set.  Enjoy! 😁 #frontlever #frontlevertraining  #calisthenicstraining #calisthenicsuk #calistenia

SORE HANDS? Make sure your GRIP is intentional ☝🏼😏 The early days of CALISTHENICS and any kind of WEIGHTLIFTING are often the most challenging due to the discomfort on the hands. The most common ways to improve the grip on the bar/equipment without roughing up one’s hands is through using GLOVES or WRAPS. LIQUID CHALK is another great way to improve your grip while slowly building up the strength in your hands.  ☝🏼 However, there is also the factor of how you actually hold the bar. A rough grip can hurt and cause blisters - which can rip - and this in turn makes progressing take longer since you have to wait for the pain to go before you can train again.  As long as you are not completely opposed to calluses - because they do improve your hang time and gripping comfort - you can still minimise the pain in the early days of training. I’m sure you all agree that times have changed and we don’t expect adults to have baby soft hands. So go train hard and be great! 😎 ✅ PRO TIP - Sliding the hand up and over the bar as you’re firmly gripping it will ensure there is no excess skin between your hand and the bar. Being intentional about this movement also allows you to brace your core and muscles in your arm and torso as you get ready to use the equipment.  This will also come in handy when moving on to FALSE GRIP territory. I will link a FG training video for now and will post a full breakdown of the skill soon. It’s such a simple thing but it can make such a difference in your early days of training. I have dropped this little nugget in here and there during workshops and many have found it useful. Additionally, as demonstrated, a little PALM STRETCH right after a painful set can also ease the discomfort. I hope these tips will be helpful to many of you and boost your progress with your training! 💪🏼☺️ #calisthenicstips #weightlifting #calluses #grip #calistenia #calisthenicstraining #calisthenicsuk #calisthenicslondon

Rings CONDITIONING for stronger muscles & SKILLS💪🏼😎 If you’ve followed me for a while then you know how important is the JOINT FORCE of your triceps and lats in most calisthenics skills. Although skills can be tough, the conditioning drills that help you get there are super scalable. 🙏🏼 ☝🏼You are limited to SKULLCRUSHERS and PULLOVERS on a bar plus needing a different height bar for all the progressions. On the rings you also have access to the additional TRICEP EXTENSION.  1️⃣The higher the rings or the further away they are from the station, the easier the exercises. Use this when you’re just starting out and are learning the movements.  2️⃣ The lower the rings or the further back you stand the harder the skills get.  3️⃣ The range between the two extremes is your playground to adjust depending on your strength levels on the day of the session or the fatigue you’re experiencing as you’re taking yourself through the workout. 4️⃣ You can use regular grip and false grip, the latter being more advanced but adding some much needed wrist and forearm strengthening to your training.  Main differences between the three demonstrated exercises: 1️⃣ SKULLCRUSHER - extending your elbows with arms in front of the body. Lower your forehead towards the rings 2️⃣ TRICEP EXTENSION - extending from the elbows with arms behind your head. Push into the rings to get them to move away from you while keeping upper arms close to head.  3️⃣ PULLOVER - essentially a combination of both, you need to drop below and take your arms behind you. Full press from the shoulders. REP RANGES: ✅ For BEGINNERS & muscle building - up to 10-12 repetitions per set, for developing good movement patterns and getting a good pump. Occasionally test a tougher setup and see if you can fatigue yourself around the 7 rep mark.  ✅ For ADVANCED skill specific strength - 3-5 reps per set at the hardest settings# and 5-7 reps per set at the easiest setting. Throw in occasionally some 1-3 rep sets to boost growth through progressive overload.  Enjoy the gains! 😏🔥 #calistenia #calisthenicsuk #calisthenicstraining #calisthenicsworkout #skullcrushers #pullover #tricepworkout

Learn to BULLWHIP your band on the bar! 💪🏼😎 Born in a casual calisthenics session back in 2020 when I just thought how awkward it was to get the band on a high bar with reaching and tiptoeing etc and I just knew there had to be a better way. 😂 So I started messing around and thought how can I just do it ‘in one’ to save time and the bullwhip method was born. 😁  You are all always so lovely and leave dozens of comments so I wanted to explain how to do it. Please feel free to learn and share the method with others! 🥰 It helps reach high bars (although you might have to climb up to get it down after 🤭) and I suppose you can aura farm with it. 😂 It’s a little harder with bigger bands like the green one as they’re chunkier but if you put more oomph behind the throw and add a powerful grab and pull, you should be able to nail it every time pretty soon.  Have fun! 😏 #calistenia #calisthenicsuk #calisthenicslondon #calisthenicstricks #tekkers #resistancebands #calisthenicstips

SWITCH UP your training with these BADASS SKILLS 💪🏼😎 Calisthenics has so much to offer, it’s not just handstands and muscleups, so it would be a shame if you didn’t even try to find out what cool skills your body is capable of! 🥹 ✅ This is a small selection of “5 YEAR SKILLS” that I am working on. I ensure the skills complement each other so that the strength is gained concurrently and my performance is boosted evenly across my repertoire. And so can you!  1️⃣ F/B LEVER COMBO - this one is accessible to BEGINNERS as you see it in the video. Use either a red or black band (I will link a video to show you how to loop it through the straps) and work on sets of 3-5 reps. You’ll want a spotter at least for your first reps/session to learn the range of movement for good depth in the back lever and you should be good to practice this twice a week. 2️⃣ IRON CROSS - I am using the arms looped method. Sometimes I place my arms below the rings, other times above. Below is harder (as seen in the video) so keep that in mind and try both if you’re INTERMEDIATE. If you are a BEGINNER, you might wish to use a red band to stand on instead to ensure you get back up from the bottom of the range. 1-3 reps per set, to fatigue in one workout, once a week.  3️⃣ B/L LADDER WALL - these conditioning skills will boost your strength and stability for B/L reps and holds. If you’re a BEGINNER, start with tuck and half tuck reps, if you’re more ADVANCED, try full Back Lever reps and holds. NB: Must lower yourself to 45 degrees. 3-6 reps per set to fatigue, once a week.  4️⃣ IMPOSSIBLE DIP - these are INTERMEDIATE/ADVANCED, however if you are already working on RUSSIAN DIPS or similar skills then this is a natural progression to the former and you might find yourself much closer to these reps than you think. Start with banded negatives and move on to unbanded negatives or banded full reps. 1-3 reps per set to fatigue, twice a week.  Head to my highlights or scroll through the videos for tutorials for all these skills.  Happy training! 🥳 #calistenia #calisthenicstraining #calisthenicsuk #ironcross #backlever #frontlever #impossibledip

NO EQUIPMENT leg workout for serious STRENGTH ✌🏼😎 When regular b/w squats and lunges don’t cut it, you need to adopt the calisthenics lower body workout. Whether you are training on holiday, outdoors or simply don’t have access to any weights, don’t worry - you can get an insane leg workout by choosing your exercises carefully.  1️⃣ SISSY SQUAT NEGATIVES - these are accessible to everyone (while the full Sissy Squat is really hard) and you can easily hold on to a chair/bench or some other sturdy item to keep your balance.  ✅ You’re hitting calves, quads, hips and glutes. Slow and controlled reps should get you 3-5 rep sets, fast tempo 7-10x. Try narrow and wide stance.  2️⃣ DRAGON SQUAT -  more of a balance challenge at first but absolutely worth giving it a go to test your mobility. You don’t have to sit down on your heel, getting thigh parallel to the ground will be tough enough.  ✅ You’re mainly hitting the quad on the standing leg with a side of glute if you’re able to go low enough. I would encourage alternating reps to manage fatigue better.  3️⃣ PISTOL SQUAT - a classic single leg exercise improving strength and balance. Aim to hit parallel to begin with and only go all the way down if you’re able to keep your heel on the ground.  ✅ Mainly hitting the quad on the standing leg with a side of glute if you’re able to remain upright and drive through the heel. If elevated leg is kept straight, this doubles as isometric hip compression work. 3-5 reps per leg per set. You can also hold a weight - this will help you stay more upright.  4️⃣ SHRIMP SQUAT - this exercises is elite for building single leg strength that also contributes to heavy weighted squats and lunges due to the transferable strength. Also very effective in knee/lower body rehab.  ✅ Quad & glute on the standing leg but also building strength and stability in ankles (as they all do). 3-5 reps per leg for slow and unassisted reps. <10 reps per leg for fast and assisted reps.  Happy training and enjoy your newly found freedom training legs anywhere! 😏 #calisthenicsworkout #bodyweigthtraining #legworkout #pistolsquat #sissysquat #shrimpsquat #dragonsquat #calistenia #legtraining

Use your DIAPHRAGM to be able to TALK or BREATHE during skills 💪🏼☺️ Most people speak from their throat and their core muscles are relaxed, which is why one’s voice becomes immediately strained during any type of more strenuous movement. Singers are the perfect example of trained diaphragms as they have learned to separate breathing from muscular contractions - they project their voice. Once it becomes second nature, it’s a sign of strong muscles and a well developed skill.  And so is the same with this. I used to be a bodybuilder for many years and I would (and will) always push myself to the point where I pull insane facial expressions, if I have to, just to get the final drop of power out of my muscles. Often times those expressions would be gritted teeth which kinda looked like a smile. 🤭  But when I started to coach calisthenics in 2020 and wanted to demonstrate skills at the same time as I was doing them, I needed to shift my focus from full body strain to controlled efforts.  ✅ The ability to talk during moving boils down to your strength. If you’re strong enough for a specific skill or have practised it for long enough, it becomes second nature. It no longer requires as much effort or focus as it did on day 1 because your body moves from muscle memory (unconscious brain) and not from what your conscious brain is telling it to do.  ✌🏼 Now don’t worry; I also have some skills during which I find it difficult to talk. Last summer Korean dips, Hefesto on rings & Iron Cross were fine to practice but tough to talk through. I have fallen out of practice with my Back Lever so we’ll find out in a few weeks time whether I have lost any strength or not. 🤭 ✅ The best way to practice? Try to hold a casual conversation during your skill or conditioning work. Last summer one of my clients discovered that she could hold a handstand much more easily when she attempted to talk. Give it a go, even if only for fun! 🥰 *The person running through the last shot, stealing my focus is a friend. 😂 #ringmuscleup #elbowlever #halfmastflag #calisthenicstraining #calisthenicsworkout #calistenia #calisthenicsuk #calisthenicslondon #caliwiththeamazon

MYTH: You need 60 minutes or more for a quality yoga practice. That’s false. You can get in a nourishing yoga practice in a shorter amount of time. Last week I felt EXHAUSTED and knew I needed to take a little break. I was short on time, so I opted for my go-to 20 minute Restorative Yoga practice. Set a timer for 5 minutes per pose.  If you don’t have 2 sets of blocks like me, you can use pillows or shoe boxes under your knees. You can use anything that gives your knees support in reclined bound angle pose. And, you can totally take this class in bed. I won’t tell 🤫 Use 2 pillows instead of the bolster and blocks. The best part of a home practice is doing your yoga wherever you want. Save this practice for the next time you need a quick little refresher in your day. Do you think tree pose is easy? Try this variation and get back to me! Tree pose is one of my favorite balancing poses because of all the variations. It’s accessible to those who have difficulty balancing (take the kickstand option and practice near a wall or chair) and to advanced yogis. In this variation, you play with bending your knee, pointing your toe and balancing before coming into tree pose. You feel the heel of your standing leg pressing firmly into the mat as you find your balance. Then, slowly open your knee out to the side and place your foot on either the mat (kickstand), your calf or above your knee. If you choose, stretch your arms out aka, “grow the branches of your tree.” Want to learn more yoga poses and variations? Sign up for my newsletter! You get a 🆓 class every month. If you have ever taken a flow class with me, you know that this is my *favorite* way to transition down to your back for savasana. In navasana (boat pose) lower down, you resist gravity as you slowly lower down from boat pose onto your back. Take a little break out of your day with me and plant my pineapple top! I am for sure an amateur gardener, haha. I do not consider myself an expert in any means, but it’s a hobby that I’ve been picking up. Sometimes I’m successful and can enjoy watching my plants bloom and grow 🌿 Other times… well, I’m not as successful, unfortunately. I have always wanted to try to grow a pineapple from a top and now I’m finally doing it!   Of course, being me, I was traveling and otherwise distracted and let this thing root for much longer than I was told. Like, 1 or 2 months longer. But, on the upside, look at all those beautiful roots! Now, hopefully, my new plant is happy in its new home and will produce a little pineapple down the line. So, why am I sharing this with you if it’s not about yoga? Well, first, because it’s fun. Second, because I think it’s important to try things that we haven’t perfected.  I think that second point actually speaks well to yoga. So many people put off starting their yoga practice or trying a certain pose because they fear they may not do it perfectly. Does that sound like you? I invite you to let go of the fear. Do not get hung up on trying to do things perfectly - just try to do them. The beauty of a consistent yoga practice is learning how to meet yourself where you are, day-to-day. The real lesson is in just taking that first step of trying. And if you fail - whether in life or in yoga - you can just pick yourself up and try the pose again. Or in my case, buy another plant. Just here to remind you to take some intuitive movement today. “What is intuitive movement?” you may ask… Well, intuitive movement is when you check with your body and move in a way that feels inherently good and natural. I often pose it to my students as “listen to what your body is asking for.” If the concept still seems allusive to you, that’s OK. We aren’t taught how to be in tune with our bodies. That’s one of the great benefits of having a consistent yoga practice. You can try moving intuitively by getting onto your yoga mat. From a seat, take some stretches that feel good to you. How do you feel? Are there other ways you would like to move? Next, try a tabletop position and try the same thing. Move in and out of cow/cow. Try child’s pose. What other poses or stretches would feel good to you right now? Try them! I always offer my students moments of intuitive movement throughout our practice. Join me on the mat to experience this way of moving with me, in person or online (check out my IG page for my current teaching schedule). Do you have a favorite way to move intuitively? DOWN HERE ⬇️ You’re in the gym, lifting weights BUT… your body still feels soft and doesn’t reflect the effort you’re putting in. I was there, putting in the work but always staying soft. Until I fixed these 3 things ❌Mistake # 1: You’re exercising, NOT training. Just holding DB’s while moving does NOT = building muscle. Classes or random YouTube workouts are great for movement, but are NOT optimal for muscle growth. Muscle is what gives you the “toned” look. Training is intentional, using challenging weights, working with intensity, getting close to failure, tracking, and applying progressive overload. We build the body in the gym, then reveal it in the kitchen. But ONLY if the work in the gym is intentional. ❌Mistake # 2: You’re using the same DB’s for upper + lower body.  Your quads and glutes are MUCH larger and stronger than your shoulders and arms. If you’re grabbing the same DB’s for shoulder presses and squats, your lower body is NOT being challenged. Muscle growth requires intensity and working close to failure. If you’re limited on equipment, slow tempo, add pauses, or increase reps to get closer to failure. But the point remains: the muscle MUST be challenged and taken close to failure. No challenge = no change. ❌Mistake #3: You’re not allowing proper rest. We were taught that workouts should be nonstop, sweaty, and exhausting. Circuits, supersets, and minimal rest. That might burn calories, but it does NOT build muscle. After doing a set, you should REST for 2-3 minutes. NOT jump into burpees or jump squats. Just rest. Let your muscles and nervous system recover so you can give your next set your best effort. This also means resting between workouts. Muscle is broken down in the gym, but it recovers and rebuilds when you REST. That means 2–3 active rest days per week and prioritizing sleep (7+ hours). If you’re guilty of any of these, don’t worry, it’s not too late to change how you train so you can finally see results from the effort you’re already putting in. What I changed👇 The rules I followed for YEARS… Eat less. Sweat more. Chase small. I started dieting in my 20s… and honestly, I never stopped. It became a viscous cycle. Lose 10–15 pounds. Gain it back. Feel like a failure. Repeat. But my body never really changed. I wasn’t getting leaner. I wasn’t getting stronger. And even when I got smaller, I was softer. Because every time I dieted harder and relied on calorie burn… I was losing muscle. And over 40, that’s a BIG problem. We’re already losing muscle with age. So if your plan is also causing muscle loss, you’re working against your body, NOT with it. For YEARS, I thought I was strength training. I was doing videos or classes, using dumbbells, doing high reps, getting sweaty and tired.  But that’s NOT how you build muscle. Muscle is built through tension, intention, and progression. That means lifting heavy enough to challenge you, controlling the tempo, getting close to or to failure, tracking and improving over time. If the weight is light, the pace is fast, and the goal is just to “feel the burn”… your body treats it like cardio, NOT a signal to build muscle. And without that signal, muscle does NOT grow. ❌So I broke the rules.❌ I started eating MORE. More protein. More whole, nourishing foods. I started fueling my body instead of depriving it. And I shifted my workouts from burning… to BUILDING. Training with intention. Progressive overload. Actually trying to get stronger. And everything changed. My body composition improved. My metabolism improved. Fat loss actually became easier. Now at 47, I’m leaner, stronger, and eating MORE than I was at 27.  That only happened when I STOPPED following the rules that worked against my body and started following rules that work with my body. Now, I train 3-4 days per week with proper strength training aka using weights that are challenging, training close to failure, and applying progressive overload. This is NOT about sweating more or “working hard.” It is about working with intention. Muscle does NOT grow because a workout feels exhausting. It grows when it is given the right stimulus, then allowed to recover and adapt. If we train too often without adequate recovery, we add stress, limit muscle growth, raise injury risk, and stall progress. Intentional training requires intentional rest for optimal results. 2️⃣ Ate MORE calories instead of less. Years of chronic dieting taught my body to survive on less. Over time, my metabolism adapted, my set point dropped, and I had to keep doing more and eating less to see any change. That is NOT sustainable or smart strategy. Strategic seasons of maintenance protect metabolism, support hormones, reduce stress, and allow you to build muscle. More muscle increases metabolic output and sets you up for easier, more sustainable fat loss later. Diets should be temporary. Maintenance is where your body heals and prepares for the next phase. This phased approach is how I help clients completely transform their bodies. DM me COACH for more info or apply with the link in my BlO.  3️⃣ Embraced carbs instead of fearing them. Carbs were something most of us were taught to avoid, but muscle LOVES carbs. They are the preferred fuel source for training and recovery. Without enough, performance suffers, recovery slows, and cortisol stays elevated. Chronically high cortisol can impact testosterone, making it easier to lose muscle and stay soft. No fuel = poor training. Poor training = less muscle. Less muscle = soft + stuck. Carbs do not make you soft. Under-fueling does. At 47, I’m leaner, stronger, eating MORE, and training LESS than I was at 27…  Which is wild considering I thought my metabolism and body would crash after 40 and in perimenopause. But what if your metabolism is NOT “slowing with age”… what if it’s the outdated methods we were taught? Here is what I thought would help me get fit versus what did! ❌ Burning as many calories as possible. You’ll NEVER “burn” your way to your best body. ✅ Building muscle is what gives a “toned” and defined body. And muscle requires strength training with progressive overload, sticking to one plan for 6-12 weeks and training close to failure sending your body a signal to change. ❌Eating as little as possible, and training fasted in attempts to burn more fat. ✅ Fueling your body, don’t starve it. You won’t burn more fat fasted and it’s the wrong mindset to have with your training. The gym is where we build; the kitchen is where we reveal. Protein and carbs pre and post workouts help performance, muscle growth and recovery. Fats throughout the day support hormones and satiety. ❌Training 6-7 days a week, the “more is more” mentality. ✅ Rest and recovery are NECESSARY for progress. You don’t need to crush yourself daily. Walking, sleep, and rest days help with recovery, fat loss, and managing stress. ❌ Letting the scale define success and thinking smaller is better. ✅ Tracking the right progress. The scale does NOT show fat loss or muscle gain accurately. Use progress photos, strength improvements, and measurements. Focus on body COMPOSITION, not just pounds. ❌ Living in a deficit. The body adapts to what you do. Chronically eating less and less, tells your body to burn less and less calories. ✅ Cycle diet phases. You’ll get better results and protect metabolism by moving through maintenance and dieting phases with intention. When you learn how to work WITH your body instead of against it you will unlock a physique you didn’t know was possible.  I know it because I’ve LIVED it and it’s what I helping other women over 40 do now. HERE!👇 Can you strength train fasted? YES. Is it optimal for building muscle and reshaping your body? Probably not. You might be thinking muscle isn’t a concern for you, because you just want to look “toned.” But being toned =  more muscle and lower body fat. Proper TRAINING is how you build that muscle, and  NUTRITION is how you support performance and recovery. The more muscle you have, the stronger, more defined, you will look. And muscle makes it easier it is to maintain results. If your goal is to be “toned”, stop viewing your gym sessions as the time to BURN, and start seeing them as the time to BUILD. Building muscle requires intensity and progression and is built through small improvements over time. ➡️One more rep ➡️2-5 more pounds ➡️Better control aka tempo. Over a month, that could mean: ✅10–20 pounds on your lifts ✅2–4 more reps per set ✅Significantly more total volume (which is one of the main drivers of muscle growth). Over a year… it’s the difference between looking like you “kinda fit” or looking strong, sculpted, and defined. While your body does have glycogen stored in your muscles for energy, it is limited. And when it’s low, performance drops.  Eating a small meal with quick-digesting carbs and protein before gives you more available energy so you can lift heavier, control tempo, and push closer to failure. If you cannot stomach food before training, try a small meal like banana and whey protein (both digest quickly). And make sure your post-workout meal includes both carbs and protein to kickstart recovery and growth. This is a big mindset shift. It took me years to stop thinking like a dieter and start thinking like an athlete. But when I did, my body got stronger, my shape improved and I felt SO much better. If you are in a calorie deficit, WHEN you eat does NOT determine fat loss, total calories does. But timing your nutrition around training can absolutely improve performance… and that’s what builds the body you want. 🚨DM me FUEL for my Fueled for Performance Guide so you know exactly what to eat before and after your workouts to train harder, recover faster, and see better results.👌 . . . #womensfitnesstips #fatlossover40 #fitover40 #perimenopausefitness

Nothing here has changed. Still 10/10 punk and hardcore albums. #onthisday #undergroundmusic #punk #hardcorepunk

A lonely-night soundtrack straight out of the neon jukebox era. Roy Orbison’s In Dreams blends heartbreak, drama, and those unreal operatic vocals into one of the defining pop records of the early ‘60s. Melancholy, dreamy, and timeless. For fans of Elvis Presley, The Everly Brothers

Boston hardcore cornerstone. Fast, pissed, youth crew before youth crew really had a name. SSD mixed early straight edge intensity with stomping riffs and a rawer, street-level feel than a lot of their peers. The Kids Will Have Their Say is essential early hardcore: urgent, aggressive, and full of that early-80s energy that made Boston a force. For fans of: Minor Threat, Negative Approach, DYS, Jerry’s Kids, Agnostic Front, Gang Green

Psychotic Tanks were an obscure 1980s German post-punk band with a cold, raw DIY sound blending anxious punk energy with minimal darkwave atmosphere. “Security Idiots / Let’s Have A Party” has that forgotten underground European punk feel; tense, weird, and catchy in all the right ways. For fans of Killing Joke, Wire, and early The Fall

Dirty, chaotic UK crossover from the early 80s mixing punk, crust, and speed metal. Raw production, loud-as-hell attitude, and pure warzone energy somewhere between Motörhead, Venom, and Discharge. For fans of Motörhead, Venom, Discharge, GBH, Amebix, early Napalm Death

Raw, pissed-off early UK punk from Bristol that sounds like it was recorded in a freezing squat with a busted amp and zero concern for polish. Fast, urgent, anti-authority stuff with that early ’80s street punk energy — rough vocals, simple riffs, and songs that feel like they’re about surviving another miserable week. One of those bands that never got huge but absolutely nails that DIY UK82 atmosphere. For fans of Discharge, Chaos UK, The Varukers, GBH, The Partisans

Obscure late ‘70s San Francisco punk that sounds completely strung out and falling apart in the best way possible. The Maggots had that perfect mix of trashy glam hooks, blown-out guitars, and real snotty first wave punk energy. Forgotten gem.  For fans of: The Ramones, Dead Boys, The Weirdos, The Avengers

Tough, swaggering British R&B with that perfect mid-60s beat sound; loud amps, sharp guitar stabs, pounding drums, and Eric Burdon sounding completely possessed behind the mic. “The Girl Can’t Help It” hits that sweet spot between bluesy bar-band chaos and early punk attitude, the kind of record that still feels reckless decades later. Pure Newcastle grit with hooks strong enough to live in your head for days. For fans of The Pretty Things, Them, early The Rolling Stones, The Kinks, The Yardbirds

One of those perfect late-70s punk obscurities that somehow slipped through the cracks. Seizure only left behind this lone 1978 ripper, but it’s exactly the kind of raw, nervous, blown-out punk record collectors obsess over decades later. Cuties Wrong Now has sharp riffs, weird energy, sneering vocals, and that totally unpolished feel that makes early punk singles so special. Released in tiny numbers on the nearly undocumented Regressive Records label, this thing still sounds wild and immediate decades later. For fans of: The Weirdos, The Kids, Electric Eels, The Adverts, early Ramones.

The Faction helped lay the groundwork for skate punk in the early 80s, mixing fast California hardcore with catchy hooks and pure skate culture energy. No Hidden Messages is raw, melodic, scrappy, and packed with that classic feel before skate punk became polished. For fans of: JFA, Agent Orange, Adolescents
